entries.section: (1) Christ and the prophets

paragraphs.text: St. Paul speaks as a Jew to his brethren the Hebrew Jews about the fathers of the Jewish people in the Old Testament, and how God's word came to them through the prophets.
In many kinds and ways: visions, dreams, appearances, and symbols of every sort, such as sacrifices and the like, and the Law with its commandments.

In this he shows the unity of the two Testaments: God is the One who speaks in the Old Testament through the prophets, and in the New Testament through Christ incarnate. And in order to show the superiority of Christ over the prophets, he confirms the Jews who had become Christians in their faith in the face of the doubts raised by their Jewish brethren and their exclusion of them from entering the Temple. So he shows that the Old Testament was a preparation for the New Testament, and that the symbols are done away with by the coming of the One they symbolize, who is greater than all the means of the Old Testament for revealing God.

entries.section: (1) Christ and the prophets

paragraphs.text: These last days: that is, the New Testament.

Whom he hath appointed heir of all things: he declared that He is the owner of all things, for He is the Creator and the Redeemer who bought us with His blood, and by His perfect righteousness He became the perfect image of man as man ought to be. The ownership of the Son is equal to the ownership of the Father, which Christ Himself declared when He said, “All things that the Father hath are mine” (Jn 16:15). By whom also he made the worlds: this shows the eternity of the Son, who at the appointed time created the worlds, the world of heaven and the world of earth.

It shows the superiority and distinction of the New Testament, since the means of speaking to mankind is no longer the prophets but God Himself incarnate, who created all creatures and then became incarnate in the fullness of time, and by His righteousness and redemption all creation became subject to Him, just as God wanted Adam to have dominion over all creation in Paradise.

entries.section: (1) Christ and the prophets

paragraphs.text: Who being: that is, Christ.

The brightness of his glory: Christ is the light of the Father, for He is Light from Light. This is a proof of the divinity of Christ, because there is no glory without brightness; He is eternal like the eternity of the glory, and does not come after it in time, as some who doubt the divinity of Christ claim.

The express image of his person: another proof of the divinity of Christ, for the image and form of God's essence appeared in the incarnate Christ; He is the very essence of God, appearing in visible form to mankind in the fullness of time. The image is not something else, or separate, or lesser, as those who use this verse to cast doubt on the divinity of Christ claim, but is the manifestation of the essence of God to mankind, as the Scripture says, “No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him” (Jn 1:18). Upholding all things: that is, the Lord Christ is the Sustainer of all things and the One who cares for them; He holds them in His hands and governs them, for He is not only their Creator but their Governor as well.

By the word of his power: His wisdom, which created all creatures, is able to do all things and governs the whole. When he had by himself purged our sins: He accomplished redemption Himself in order to cleanse all who believe in Him from their sins; He is the One who works by Himself in the New Testament, and not through another, as in the Old Testament.

Sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high: the right hand represents blessing and power, and does not mean a particular direction, because God is unlimited and has neither right nor left. What is meant is that Christ, after His resurrection, ascended into the heavens to be in His glory which He had from eternity and which He hid by His incarnation and humility in order to accomplish our redemption; that is, the divine majesty became manifest to mankind in the heights, that is, the heavens, which is everything that is exalted above our minds and our material thoughts.

St. Paul continues his discourse about Christ, who is God, the Creator and Governor of all that exists, and who became incarnate and emptied Himself in order to accomplish the redemption of mankind, and then ascended into heaven. In this the greatness of Christ and of Christianity appears over Judaism, which symbolizes it and prepares the way for it.

God desires to speak with you always, and in His wisdom He seeks the way by which you will respond, whether through events around you, or people close to you, or His voice in the Holy Bible, so that you may repent and return to Him; and out of His abundant love He gives you Himself in His Body and Blood on the altar. So do you, beloved, enjoy these revelations that call you to His embrace, or do you still think of God as an obscure God, incomprehensible, far from you and set apart in His heaven?

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: Being made: this does not mean change, but that Christ, after accomplishing redemption, regained His glory which He had voluntarily set aside.
Inherited: this indicates that the Lord Christ possesses all the authority that God the Father has (Jn 3:35). Name: standing.

By the ascension of Christ His eternal divine glory appeared, which is greater than the glory of the angels whom He created in heaven, for He is God, the Owner of all creatures, whereas the angels possess superior abilities in understanding, movement and work which God gave them.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: Unto which of: a style that denies with all certainty that any of the angels is equal to the Lord Christ, to Him be glory, and this refutes the doctrine of the Adventists or the Jehovah's Witnesses that the Lord Christ is the angel Michael. This day: what is meant is before all ages.

Here he speaks of the eternity of the Son, begotten of the Father before all ages, quoting this from (Ps 2:7) and also (Ps 89:26, 27). He is equal to the Father in essence, whereas the angels are creatures whom God created at a particular time, just as He created the rest of mankind. And of course our sonship to God by adoption is different from the Son's sonship to the Father in essence.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: And again, when he bringeth in: the Father sent the Son and brought Him into the world by the Incarnation. This does not mean the separation of the Father from the Son, for they are one in essence, and this is a movement within the divine Self, just as a man sends from his mind a signal to one of his members, such as his hand or his foot, to move; he is not two but one man.

The firstbegotten: the Divine inspiration, through the tongue of St. Paul, means that when the Son became incarnate and entered into the world, He set aside the glory that was His. Therefore he used the word firstborn, which indicates that Christ as man is the firstborn of all who believe in Him; He is the God who became man, who presented to us the new man in place of fallen Adam. This of course does not mean that He is merely a created man, but that in His humility He became incarnate to become, by His pure human nature, the firstborn for everyone who believes in Him; and He is the firstborn of creation, that is, its head, and not the first created.

Let all the angels of God worship him: the Divine inspiration brought this testimony from (the Book of Deuteronomy 32:43) according to the Septuagint translation of the Holy Bible, confirming that the angels worship the Son, for it is self-evident that the One worshipped is greater than the one who offers worship.
The distinction of Christ from the angels appears in that when He became incarnate the angels worshipped Him, because they know that He is God, their Creator and the Creator of all that exists.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: Winds: as a comparison, that they are an instrument in the hand of God which He uses for His will, and they (the angels) are not themselves merely wind (Jon 1:4). A flame of fire: because they are spirits kindled with the fire of divine love, he likens them to a flame of fire; and what is meant is what he mentioned, that they are servants and instruments in His divine hand.

St. Paul brought comparisons for the angels which he took from (Ps 104:4), namely the winds and the flame of fire, to declare that both are creatures created by the Son, like the angels, to affirm that the angels are created and are not like the Son, of whom he says, “Thy throne, O God”...

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: Thy throne: your throne, and the meaning of the verse is that your kingdom is everlasting forever.
A sceptre: the sceptre of rule, and the meaning is that the order of your kingdom is uprightness.
On the other hand he shows that Christ is God, the King of kings, who rules the whole world forever, and the angels are merely His servants, as (Ps 45:6) mentions.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity: righteousness is a constant attribute in the Lord Christ, which does not change in Him and which He does not lose for any reason, because it is not given to Him by another, like the angels, whose righteousness is given by God, and the proof of this is the fall of a number of the angels who became demons (Jude 6). God hath anointed thee: its meaning is that He set you apart to accomplish redemption.
Thy God: with respect to the humanity.
Above thy fellows: all the anointed kings and prophets; and he means in general all creatures, whom He became incarnate to resemble in everything except sin.

Kings used to be anointed with oil, and each one of them who was anointed was called “the Lord's anointed.” The phrase above thy fellows here means the distinction of our Lord Jesus Christ from all the kings and prophets who came before Him, as (Ps 45:7) mentions. They are His fellows with respect to the mission of preaching, warning and proclaiming the voice of God, but the special anointing of Christ relates to His redemption and His salvation of us, which no one else can accomplish, because He is distinguished from all mankind and the angels by perfect righteousness and perfect joy; He is the source of all joy in the world for all creatures, whether angels or men.

Do you love righteousness, so that you strive to acquire the virtues? May you also care about works of mercy, seizing every opportunity to do good. This will gradually take you away from your evil thoughts and from all sin; indeed, the more you enjoy life with God, the more you will hate sin.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: In the beginning: the time of the beginning of the creation of the world.

The Divine inspiration affirmed in (Ps 102:25-27) the attribute of creation in the Lord Christ, and this is evidence of the oneness of the Father and the Son, because God alone is the Creator, and David called Him “O Lord,” affirming His divinity. In this psalm he speaks about Christ, the Savior of mankind, who is the Creator of the whole world, heaven with all the angels and creatures in it, and earth with all the people and beings on it.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: The psalm declares that all creatures will pass away on the last day, and likens them to a garment which by its nature wears out and decays when time passes over it. It also likens creatures to a vesture that God folds up, so that it becomes a piece of cloth that is no longer used; but Christ, on the other hand, is not touched by change, for He is eternal and created all these creatures at a particular time, the time He created the world, and He lives forever. Thus the superiority of Christ over the angels and all creatures appears.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: My right hand: it signifies power and perfect divine glory, for God has neither right nor left.
Thine enemies: all who refuse to believe in you and become against you.

The psalm (110:1) declares the Father's words to the Son after He accomplished redemption, saying, “The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand,” that is, to you belongs all power and you are established in it, and everyone who opposes you is subject to you. This is unique to Christ alone and cannot be said of any angel, because he is a creature, whereas Christ is God, all-powerful and almighty.

entries.section: (2) Christ and the angels

paragraphs.text: Because the Lord Christ is seated on the throne, He has authority over all the angels to send them as created spirits to serve and attend to the needs of the people who have resolved to live with Him and to enjoy the inheritance of eternal life. Christ is God, whereas the angels are His servants.

Yes, heavenly Love, the God who entrusted my salvation, mine the sinner, to no one but His only Son. What love is this, my God, with which You loved me, so that You set Yourself apart for my sake, reigning in my heart with uprightness and righteousness and the hatred of iniquity, founding and establishing the earth for me to walk upon, and then declaring to me: do not cling to it or be attached to it, for it perishes and passes away. You send Your angels to serve me, who long for Your salvation. Beloved, grant me a heart overflowing with thanksgiving for Your boundless graces in the person of Your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, that I may live rejoicing and glad in You here on earth until I reach perfect rejoicing in heaven.

A comparison between Christ and the angels as it appears in (Heb 1). Aspect: the Lord Christ; the angels. The comparison. Nature: one with the Father in essence; luminous spirits. “Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee” (v. 5); “Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire” (v. 7); “I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son” (v. 5); “ministering spirits” (v. 14). Worship: Christ is the One worshipped by the angels; the angels offer worship to God. “And let all the angels of God worship him” (v. 6). Creator: Christ is the Creator; created spirits like the rest of nature. “By whom also he made the worlds” (v. 2); “Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire” (v. 7); “Thou, Lord (the Son), in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands” (v. 10); “ministering spirits” (v. 14). Eternity: Christ is eternal, begotten of the Father before all ages; the angels are created, having a beginning in time. “Who maketh his angels” (v. 7); “Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee” (v. 5). Righteousness: Christ is God the Righteous, free from all error in Himself; creatures liable to error, as proved by the fall of some of them, who are the demons.

“Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity” (v. 9). Authority: Christ has all the authority that God has; the angels are sent by God for service. “But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?” (v. 13); “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister” (v. 14). Constancy: Christ, to Him be glory, is constant and does not change, and is eternal in Himself; for the angels, their constancy is from God, and their immortal and eternal life is a gift from God.

“They shall perish; but thou remainest” (v. 11); “Thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail” (v. 12). The incarnate Christ our Savior. St. Paul continues the discourse that came in the first chapter and draws from it an important application, which is to give heed to the salvation that was accomplished on the Cross. Then he begins to prove the necessity of the appearance of the Lord Christ in this humble form, that is, lower than the angels, for the sake of our salvation.

entries.section: (1) Holding fast to the salvation of Christ offered to us

paragraphs.text: The things which we have heard: the teachings of Christianity.
Lest we should let them slip: we know them in theory and then neglect to apply them in our lives.

If Christ is greater than the angels, then we ought to give heed to the teachings of Christianity about the salvation offered on the Cross, which is greater and more perfect than the teachings of the Old Testament delivered by the hands of angels, so that we may apply them and live by them.

entries.section: (1) Holding fast to the salvation of Christ offered to us

paragraphs.text: The word spoken by angels: the Law which Moses received from God by the hands of angels (Acts 7:53, Gal 3:19). If the word of God given to Moses through angels was strong and steadfast and could not be changed, because it was from God and whoever transgressed it was punished, as appeared in the history of the Jewish people when they neglected the Law and received severe punishments such as the captivity, how much more shall he be punished who neglects the salvation offered by Christ Himself, the Word of God, who became incarnate and redeemed us on the Cross and taught us His commandments Himself, and then the disciples and Apostles, who heard His teachings themselves and saw His crucifixion and resurrection, explained His teachings to us. This salvation is greater and more perfect than the salvation offered in the law of the Old Testament, because in the Old Testament the word of God was by the hands of angels, but in the New Testament Christ, the Word of God Himself, saves mankind by His redemption. And Christ confirmed this salvation when He strengthened His disciples and Apostles with miracles and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, such as preaching and speaking in tongues.

May you think of the love of Christ the Redeemer, crucified for your sake, and let it be the center of your daily life, so that you meditate on Him and thank Him, that your heart may be reassured of Christ's care for you, and respond to His love with many prayers, and with service and mercy toward those around you.

entries.section: (2) The submission of believers to Christ

paragraphs.text: The world to come: the believers in the Church, and then in eternity.

The Jews believed that the archangel Michael was responsible for the care of the Jewish people, and that the other peoples were under the care of other angels. But in the New Testament the believers in the Church enjoy not only the care of the angels but also the salvation of Christ Himself, who is the Head of the Church, and then their submission to Him is completed in eternity, where the power of Satan is abolished and they belong to Christ with their whole being in continual praise.

entries.section: (2) The submission of believers to Christ

paragraphs.text: One: the prophet David in (Ps 8:4). The prophet David speaks of weak, fallen humanity in need of salvation, expressing it by “man,” and how God cared for its salvation and visited it by sending His only Son Jesus Christ incarnate, who took the form of the Son of Man as a human being, setting aside His divine glory in order to redeem mankind. So, while in the form of man, He was lower than the angels, and this humility was for a short time, namely the period of His Incarnation, and after it He accomplished redemption and rose from the dead and ascended into the heavens, and appeared in the crown of glory and honor which was His from eternity, and gave salvation to those who believe in Him, who are the work of His hands and are subject to Him because He bought them with His blood.

These words apply not only to Christ but also to the spiritual man who believes in Him, for Christ gives him grace and awe in the eyes of others, so that they esteem him and feel his greatness because of his inner peace and the work of God with him, although he appears in many seasons to be in a state of weakness and enduring sufferings; then God's glory for him is completed when he receives the heavenly crown.

entries.section: (2) The submission of believers to Christ

paragraphs.text: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet: this is the text of the psalm (Ps 8:6). Things: the Gentiles, for the believers from all the Gentiles have submitted to Him.

Christ died for the redemption of all mankind, Jews and Gentiles; all who believe in Him have submitted to Him, and not only the Jewish people. But the Apostle then adds that in the world there are still many who refuse to believe in Christ and do not submit to Him, because submission will be completed in eternity, when the believers are glorified in the Kingdom and the unbelievers are punished in eternal torment.

Give me, my Lord Jesus, the grace of submission to You, for in submission to You is all life. Grant that I may not share with the world in its sins, for which it rejects You, but let all my words and deeds be according to Your commandments, and let my thoughts also be pure before You, so that You may be glorified in me and I may be a light in Your hand to the world around me.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels: Jesus Christ in His Incarnation humbled Himself and appeared lower than the angels in honor.

Crowned with glory and honour: by His resurrection and ascension into the heavens. Christ was also crowned with the crown of love on the Cross and the crown of victory over Satan by His death, for by His death He trampled down death.
For the suffering of death: because He endured all the sufferings of the Cross and death, He rose crowned with glory and honor.
By the grace of God: the power of Christ's divinity, which sustained Him in enduring the sufferings and death.

That he should taste death: he did not say die but taste death, that is, He died for a short time, three days, so that those who believe in Him would not fear death, for it is the bridge of their crossing to the blessed eternity through Christ's redemption of them. For every man: Christ's death and redemption were for everyone who believes in Him, to receive salvation. So instead of man dying, Christ died for him, that he might live in Christ.

Christ humbled Himself by His Incarnation and became like us and endured suffering and death for us, and then His glory appeared by His resurrection and ascension, so that we would not fear death and would trust in the crowns that await us if we remain steadfast in faith in Him.

Your way to experience spiritual consolations and God's blessings in your life is through enduring the sufferings of life with thanksgiving for God's sake, and you can experience greater depths in fellowship with God when you endure sufferings in place of others, such as the labors of service, or bearing accusations over mistakes made by someone else, without defending yourself so as to cover for him. This is the way of redemption which Christ made for your sake, so you make it for the sake of others, and then Christ reveals Himself to you in a way you have not known before.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: It became him: the Jews were waiting for a Messiah to save them from the Romans, and they stumbled when He suffered and was crucified and died; so Paul answers that the Father wants these sufferings to be accomplished in His Son for the salvation of mankind. This is what is fitting in the sight of God.
Him: God the Father.
For whom are all things: the only purpose of creation is to praise and glorify God.
By whom are all things: all creation was created by the hand of God.
Many sons: those who believe in Christ.
Glory: the blessings of the New Testament in the Church, and then the glories of the Kingdom.

To make perfect ... through sufferings: Christ completes His saving work by enduring all the sufferings of the Cross and death in order to redeem mankind; this is the desire of the heart of the Father and the Son, that His children be saved from death.
The captain of their salvation: the Maker of salvation for all believers, that is, Christ.

It shows the participation of the Father and the Son in accomplishing redemption in that the Father, who is the Creator of all mankind and the goal of their life and who seeks their salvation, saw fit to give up His beloved Son for the redemption of His children who would believe in Him, completing every punishment of sin on their behalf and paying the debt before divine justice, so that He gives them complete salvation.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: He that sanctifieth: Christ, who set Himself apart for the salvation of those who believe in Him.
They who are sanctified: those who believe in Christ, who have dedicated their lives to God and received their salvation.
One: God the Creator of all, or Adam the father of all mankind.

The humility of Christ in His Incarnation, which made Him for a little while lower than the angels, enabled Him to share the flesh with those who believe in Him, and He united with them in the origin, who is Adam, so He became a man like them, and likewise He united with them in sonship to God, but with a difference, since Christ is the Son of God by nature and essence, whereas men are sons by adoption. And since He shared humanity with men, He is not ashamed, despite His unlimited divine greatness, to call those who believe in Him brethren. By this He raised all believers to the sonship of God, though they are merely His creatures; but through the Incarnation they became brethren of Christ and sons of God.

It is wondrous humility on Your part, O God, to call me, the lowly one, Your brother; yet I rejoice, for this honor encourages me to draw near to You in prayer; and on the other hand it urges me to call all who are younger than I in age or lower in rank my brethren and to treat them with all love and humility, as You treat me.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: The church: it is the Church of the New Testament, and in the original of the psalm “the congregation” was written, that is, the congregation of believers, which is the Church.

Paul confirms his words with a verse from the Old Testament (Ps 22:22), which speaks in the voice of Christ, who preached to mankind and gave them salvation and called them His brethren because of His sharing the flesh with them, and then they share with Him in praising God within the Church, which is His Body.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: The Apostle quotes from (Isa 8:17) a prophecy about Christ, who by His Incarnation shared with mankind, so He speaks on their behalf to God in putting trust in Him, that we may receive by His grace obedience to God and trust in Him in everything.

He also quotes from (Isa 8:18) a prophecy about the incarnate Christ the Redeemer, who addresses those who believe in Him as a father, and presents them as His children before the Father to unite them with Himself so that they live with Him forever. And he said “again” twice in this verse because the first meaning is that Christ is a representative of mankind and the second is that He is a father to it.

The way to God has become easy through Christ, who gives us boldness and confidence in our relationship with Him, and teaches us how to obey Him and wait for Him however long our petition is delayed and our problems increase, so that we trust in Him, confident of His fatherhood and love, and press on Him in faith so as to experience Him more than before.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: The children: mankind.
Flesh and blood: human nature; this confirms the humanity of Christ and refutes all the heresies that reject this.
Destroy: make void.
The devil: the accuser.

A new benefit which mankind received by the Incarnation of Christ, which is the abolition of the authority of eternal death over those who believe in Him, for by His death He trampled down death, and the devil, the accuser of mankind, no longer has authority to take them after death to hell and eternal torment with him, because Christ by His Incarnation and redemption set them free and gave them life with Him in Paradise and the Kingdom.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: Them: all mankind.

The Incarnation of Christ proclaimed the union of God with man as a preparation for his redemption by the Cross, to set free His children, mankind, who were sentenced to death because of their sins. And in their fear of eternal death they became enslaved to the devil, and this drove them to fall into various sins. So the Incarnation of Christ frees them from the authority of the devil and the fear of death and every sin.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: He took on him: does not rescue.
Angels: those who fell, that is, the demons.
The seed of Abraham: everyone who has the faith of Abraham, whether Jews or Gentiles.

The incarnate Christ the Redeemer did not come to save the demons, because they refuse repentance and persist in sin and tempt man and make him fall in open defiance of God, but He became incarnate to save the people who believe in Him, and since they have the faith of Abraham He calls them the seed of Abraham with respect to faith and not the flesh; He saves the Jews and the Gentiles, but he said Abraham because he is speaking to the Hebrews and Abraham is the father of faith acknowledged among them.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: Wherefore: therefore.
In all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren: Christ becomes a perfect man, body and soul, so that He is like the rest of mankind, and in humility He calls them His brethren.

Another reason for the Incarnation of Christ is that men may feel that He is like them in their human nature, so they feel His tenderness toward them and His nearness to them, and He gives them their needs and feels their sufferings. Then He comes forward as the High Priest of the New Testament, not to make atonement, like the high priest in the Old Testament, by sprinkling the blood of animals on the ark of God's covenant, but He offers His blood on the Cross to take away our sins, and in this He is faithful in accomplishing redemption and delivering His people from death and supporting them in all their afflictions.

entries.section: (3) The blessings of the Incarnation

paragraphs.text: Christ endured in His life on earth many sufferings, whether by direct temptations from Satan to make Him fall into pride and the lusts of the world, or by enduring insults, torments and persecutions up to the Cross, so that every person in temptation and affliction feels that Christ suffered the pains of temptations like him, and feels with him and sympathizes with him and supports him and comforts him during the temptation.

If God sympathizes with you in your afflictions, may you make those around you feel your sympathy with them. Merely listening to their complaints or encouraging them with kind words comforts their souls, how much more if you complete your love for them with works of mercy and help, so that they rejoice with you.
It is noticed from the foregoing that Christ gave us many blessings by His Incarnation, which are:
1- Our being called brethren of Christ.
2- Praising God in Christ and with His help.
3- Trusting in God and obeying Him.
4- Sonship to God.
5- Not fearing death.
6- Being strengthened in temptations because Christ is with us and feels with us.
Comparison between Christ and Moses

entries.section: (1) Christ and Moses

paragraphs.text: Wherefore: based on what was mentioned before in the second chapter.
Brethren: Paul feels his fellowship with the Jews who became Christians in the Body of Christ.
Holy: the Christians, because they are dedicated to Christ.

The heavenly calling: the calling of Christ, which he describes as heavenly because He came down from heaven and will raise us to Him in heaven, in Paradise and the Kingdom, and also because His commandments are lofty and spiritual.
Consider: that is, contemplate and understand the saving work of Christ.

The Apostle of our profession: Christ, sent from the Father to us by His Incarnation so that we may see God before us and confess and believe in Him, and Christ declared, saying, “He that hath seen me hath seen the Father” (Jn 14:9). The sending of the Son does not mean His separation from the Father, but He is with Him at all times and fills every place despite His Incarnation.

High Priest: Christ is the High Priest of the New Testament, who offered the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross as an atonement for our sins, in place of the high priest in the Old Testament, who offered on one day in the year, the Day of Atonement, the blood of animals and sprinkled it on the ark of the covenant as a symbol of the blood of Christ the Redeemer. Because the Lord Christ is able to help those who are tempted, therefore, brethren in Christ Jesus, who made us all brethren in Him, you who have been called to enjoy heavenly joy, look closely and contemplate our Lord Jesus Christ, this One who came to connect us with heaven, who came to take our confession of the true faith and enter with it into the Holy of Holies of heaven itself, and not like the high priest in the Old Testament, who was in the Aaronic priesthood (Deut 26:3).

entries.section: (1) Christ and Moses

paragraphs.text: Appointed him: the Father sent the Son into the world to redeem it, and this does not mean the separation of the Son from the Father, because they are one in essence, and His being sent means the Incarnation and not His moving from one place to another, because despite His Incarnation He still fills every place with His divinity.
His house: His people, whom He shepherded and led in the wilderness for 40 years.

The Lord Jesus was faithful to God in the mission for which He came, just as Moses was faithful among the people of the children of Israel. It is noticed that St. Paul did not begin by preferring Christ to Moses, because Moses is the greatest of the prophets of the children of Israel, so he began by speaking of the likeness of Christ in faithfulness to Moses: Christ accomplished redemption on the Cross as Moses accomplished the shepherding of his people, and in the following verses he showed the superiority of Christ to Moses.

entries.section: (1) Christ and Moses

paragraphs.text: This man: Christ.
The house: the people of Israel, of whom Moses was one of the members.
This noble Person, that is, our Lord Jesus Christ, is worthy of much more glory than Moses by the same difference of glory between God the builder of the house and the house.

entries.section: (1) Christ and Moses

paragraphs.text: The house: the tabernacle of the congregation, that is, the temple of the Old Testament.

The greatness of Moses comes from his building of the tabernacle of the congregation, but Christ is the Creator of all mankind, among them Moses, and He is responsible for the redemption of all mankind and not only the people of Israel. Moses is a faithful servant of God, but Christ is God Himself, the Creator of all and the Redeemer of all.

entries.section: (1) Christ and Moses

paragraphs.text: As a servant, for a testimony: he completes his service, which prepares for and bears witness to Christ who comes after him.
Those things which were to be spoken after: the teachings of Christ.
As a son over his own house: the Master and Owner of everything, because He is the Creator and the Redeemer, and He is the Head of the Church and its Savior.

The faithfulness of Moses was a faithfulness entrusted to him as a servant in the tabernacle of the congregation and for the shepherding of the children of Israel, but the faithfulness of the Lord Christ over the souls of mankind, which is us, is the faithfulness of the Owner of everything, because He is God the Creator and Redeemer. And we Christians will enjoy the blessings of His faithfulness and His great redeeming work for our sake if we remain steadfast in confidence in His person and hold fast the hope which the Lord Jesus gives us.
So when St. Paul compared the difference of glory between our Lord Jesus Christ and the prophet Moses, we can say that he compared in two basic respects:
A - The breadth of the faithfulness of the person of our Lord Jesus Christ (the Builder of all) compared with Moses and his faithfulness over the house of Israel.
B - The authority of the Lord Jesus as a Son in His house (the whole) and the work of Moses as a servant in the house of Israel.

May you hold fast to your hope in God however troubles surround you or the devil's wars increase against you or your falls multiply, for Christ is able to raise you up from all these; and if you suffer and endure, lift your eyes to the hope of eternity, in which your Christ will compensate you with inexpressible joys and glories.

entries.section: (2) Hardness of heart

paragraphs.text: Wherefore: because you are children of God who believe in Him, as the preceding verse indicates.

The Holy Ghost: through the mouth of David in (Ps 95:7-11). To day: he means the literal meaning, that is, today for the hearer when God speaks to him in the Holy Bible or alerts him by any means, so that he does not neglect it or disobey.
Harden: the heart means the center of the emotions, so that man should not make his heart stiff, devoid of feelings toward the word of God, and reject it.
The provocation: murmuring and intense anger.

The day of temptation: the day on which the children of Israel murmured against Moses because there was no water, and he struck the rock before them and it brought forth water, and the place was named Meribah or Massah (Ex 17:1-7). And Psalm (95) mentions the name Meribah to clarify the meaning of the day of temptation. What is meant here is not only the murmuring of the children of Israel at Meribah but their repeated murmuring in the wilderness of Sinai and before crossing into it.
The wilderness: the wilderness of Sinai.

St. Paul moves from the relation of Christ to Moses to His relation to His people, the Jews who became Christians, and calls them to obey Him and believe His teachings and not to doubt and murmur because of the ideas of the unbelieving Jews, and not to imitate their forefathers when they murmured against God before they crossed the Red Sea and during their wandering in the wilderness of Sinai when they were thirsty or found bitter water or grew weary of the manna ... etc. (Ex 14:11, Ex 16:3).

entries.section: (2) Hardness of heart

paragraphs.text: Tempted me: tested me.
Proved me: they saw My care and concern for them and My ability to do miracles for them.

The children of Israel believed in God, the God of their fathers, but in the wilderness of Sinai they came to know God through His care and His provision for their needs and His leading of them, and that for a long time, forty years, but unfortunately throughout this period they tested God and angered Him and murmured many times, and He was patient and poured out His blessings upon them.

entries.section: (2) Hardness of heart

paragraphs.text: Wherefore: because of their testing of Me and their murmuring and their doubting My power.
I was grieved: I hated.
This generation: the people of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai, and what is meant is their sins and not their persons, since He continued to shepherd them in the hope that they would repent.

They do alway err in their heart: they doubt and murmur, so their hearts turn away from Me and they think of material things. They have not known my ways: they did not believe and walk in a spiritual way of obedience and trust.

God was angry because of the people's murmuring against Him and their preoccupation with material things away from Him, so they did not live with Him, although the purpose of setting them apart as His people and bringing them out of Egypt was to devote themselves to the worship of God and to enjoy fellowship with Him, far from the disturbance of the idol worship in Egypt.

entries.section: (2) Hardness of heart

paragraphs.text: I sware: the prophet David in the psalm likens God to man in the oath, that is, the word which one does not go back on, in order to clarify the necessity of the fulfillment of God's word.
My rest: the Promised Land.

Because of the children of Israel's persistence in murmuring and unbelief, God decided to deprive them of entering the Promised Land, so He made them wander in the wilderness of Sinai forty years until all the adults who were attached to the land of Egypt died, and the children who were raised in the wilderness remained, and learned the worship of God and endured the hardships of the wilderness and saw God's care and believed in Him, so they deserved to enjoy His good things in the Promised Land. And none of the adults entered with them except two, who were distinguished by faith, namely Joshua and Caleb.

God calls you by different means, whether by His good things and gifts so that you thank Him, or by afflictions so that you take refuge in Him, or by His commandments, written or heard, so that you take heed and live with Him. So do not neglect His voice, but let today be an opportunity for you for repentance and renewing your covenants with Him, and He will pour out on you blessings you cannot imagine and you will delight in experiencing fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: St. Paul moves from his talk about the hardness of the hearts of the children of Israel and their murmuring in the wilderness to his purpose, which is to confirm the faith of the Jews who became Christians, so he warns them lest any man keep evil in his heart by doubting the Christian faith or accepting the words of the Jews who make them feel their deprivation of Jewish worship as though they had lost their relationship with God, so that none may return to Judaism because of these doubts but remain steadfast in his faith in Christ.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: Exhort one another: admonish one another.
Daily: seizing every opportunity to confirm one another's faith.
While it is called To day: as long as there is an opportunity for repentance and life with God. The deceitfulness of sin: the lusts of sin and the pride that may result from them.

The Apostle Paul warns the believers to encourage one another so that they remain steadfast in faith in Christ, seizing every opportunity for teaching and preaching so that they do not lose their spiritual feelings toward God and fall into evil lusts and the pride into which the Jews fell because of their pride in being the chosen people and better than all mankind, so that they rejected Christ and faith in Him.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: Partakers of Christ: our sharing in the faith and its blessings by our membership in the Church.
The beginning of our confidence: the faith with which we began.

He clarifies the greatness of the blessings which the believers enjoy in the Church, since they have become members in the Body of Christ and receive the Holy Sacraments and enjoy the means of grace such as prayers and fasts. All this if they remain until the end of their lives in the upright faith with which they began and do not listen to the doubts of the Jews.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: He also reminds them to continue in their spiritual life and their living feelings toward God, so that they do not fall into murmuring and anger against God because of material lusts.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: Provoked: angered God or made Him angry with them.

Although God brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by great miracles, the ten plagues, and divided the Red Sea before them, yet they went back and angered Him because of their murmuring and their disobedience in entering the Promised Land.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: God hated the murmurings of the children of Israel and their unbelief and disobedience to Him in entering the Promised Land, so He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, in which all the adults died and their bodies were buried in the wilderness of Sinai, and they did not enter the Promised Land except Joshua and Caleb.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: Believed not: they did not obey the word of God, that is, they did not believe it so as to obey it.
Because of the unbelief of the children of Israel and their murmuring, God decided to deprive them of entering the Promised Land.

entries.section: (3) Faith

paragraphs.text: St. Paul summarizes and states that unbelief is the reason for the deprivation of the children of Israel from enjoying God's promises in entering the Promised Land, which means their enjoying fellowship with Him and is a type of the heavenly Canaan.

Your continual relationship with God in the prayers and readings of every day confirms your faith in Him, so it is easy for you to obey His commandments. So seize every opportunity to be with God in the church and in your closet, and you will enjoy fellowship with Him on earth and in heaven.

A comparison between the rest in the land of Canaan and the rest in Christ. In this chapter a comparison between the rest on the Sabbath day and Joshua, who brought the people of God into rest in the Promised Land, and Christ, who brings those who believe in Him into the true rest in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (1) The rest is not accomplished on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: A promise left us of entering into his rest: God's promise to believers of eternal rest.
Come short of it: that is, not obtain it.

God promised His people in ancient times that they would enter the Promised Land, and not all the people obtained this promise, because most of those who murmured and refused to enter fell and died in the wilderness of Sinai. So the Apostle warns us of the necessity of caution lest we fail to obtain God's promise of rest like those who did not enter.

The fear of God gives you carefulness and distance from sin, so you receive God's mercies and support, and it urges you on to spiritual striving, so that by the grace of God you secure a place in the Kingdom. Remember God, who sees you, when the thought of sin fights you, so that you quickly move away from it.

entries.section: (1) The rest is not accomplished on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: The word preached: God's promise and good news to His people in ancient times of entering the Promised Land.

St. Paul warns us that we have heard the good news of Christ the Savior as the Jews heard in ancient times the good news of entering the Promised Land, but most of them did not enter because of their unbelief and their murmuring against Moses, so they died in the wilderness (Num 14:1-3).

entries.section: (1) The rest is not accomplished on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: The works were finished from the foundation of the world: God's creation of the world, including the Promised Land, and likewise the Kingdom of Heaven.

We who believe enter into eternal rest because of our faith in Christ, but the people of Israel in ancient times did not enter the Promised Land because of their unbelief, although God had finished the creation of everything before He created man.

entries.section: (1) The rest is not accomplished on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: The first announcement of rest in the Holy Bible was on the seventh day (Gen 2:2), when God finished the creation of the world. The rest here does not mean ceasing from work, but God's joy in what He had made, because Christ says, “My Father worketh hitherto, and I work” (Jn 5:17).

entries.section: (1) The rest is not accomplished on the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: In this place: that is, on the Sabbath day, which was a type of the eternal rest.
The Jews did not enjoy rest on the Sabbath day because they:
1- Understood rest to mean ceasing from work and not doing good.
2- Did not believe in Christ the Savior, who is the Lord of the Sabbath and the Giver of true rest.
Faith in Christ gives you reassurance in all your steps, and makes you feel the sweetness of fellowship with Him and leads you to the constant enjoyment of eternity.

entries.section: (2) The rest is not completed in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: Seeing therefore it remaineth: there is something other than the rest of the Sabbath and the land of Canaan, and it is the Kingdom of Heaven. Some must enter therein: those who believe in Christ.
They to whom it was first preached: the Jews whom Moses called to enter the Promised Land and who refused because of their unbelief in the power of God that overcomes the enemies before them.
Entered not in because of unbelief: they did not enter the Promised Land because of their disobedience to God by the hand of Moses.

It is understood from the foregoing that those who believe in Christ will enter the heavenly Kingdom, whereas the children of Israel, whom God called to enter the Promised Land as a type of entering the Kingdom of Heaven, murmured and did not obey God, so they did not enter.

entries.section: (2) The rest is not completed in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: Again, he limiteth a certain day: a day in which the rest of the Kingdom is promised.

Saying in David: that is, in the Book of Psalms, most of which David wrote (Ps 95:7, 8). To day, after so long a time: the day is the days of David, which is after a period of about 500 years from the children of Israel's entering the Promised Land. David is of course speaking of another rest than the Promised Land which they had entered before.

As it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts: David calls to all mankind that if they hear the good news of Christ the Savior, they should not harden their hearts and reject it, lest they be deprived of entering the Kingdom of Heaven.
Because the true rest is in the Kingdom of Heaven, David, who lived a long time after the entering of the Promised Land, calls to mankind to believe in Christ the Savior, who gives them eternal life.

entries.section: (2) The rest is not completed in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: Paul affirms that if the true rest were in the land of Canaan by the hand of Joshua, David would not have spoken about another rest which we enter by faith in Christ if we hear the good news of Him.

entries.section: (2) The rest is not completed in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: It is understood from the foregoing that there is another rest for the people of God, that is, the Jews, which is neither the Sabbath nor the land of Canaan, and it is the eternal rest which the new people of God receive, that is, those who believe in Christ the Savior.

entries.section: (2) The rest is not completed in the Promised Land

paragraphs.text: For he that is entered into his rest: the believer in Christ who has entered into eternity.
Hath ceased from his own works: the works of spiritual striving and the labors of this life.

As God did from his: as God rested on the seventh day after completing the creation of the world and rejoiced in what He had completed, so also the believers when they enter heaven rejoice in being with God after their striving on earth.
The believer in Christ who enters the blessed eternity enjoys true rest, like the rest which God feels after completing the creation of the world, which is spiritual rest.

Do not be much preoccupied with the comfort and pampering of your body, for all this is temporary and passing. As much as you are able, give yourself the opportunity to pray and serve even at the partial expense of the body's comfort, and you will enjoy fellowship with God.

entries.section: (3) Striving to enter the rest

paragraphs.text: Since we have been assured that true rest is in Christ the Savior, who gives it to us in the heavens, let us strive spiritually to leave every sin and hold fast to faith and a life of righteousness so that we have a place in heaven, and not fall into disobedience to God's commandments as the Jews disobeyed in ancient times, but take warning from their unbelief.

entries.section: (3) Striving to enter the rest

paragraphs.text: What helps us in striving is that the words of God in the Holy Bible are:
Quick, and powerful: they do not grow old but are always strong and affect souls.
Sharper than any twoedged sword: very sharp, more than the two-edged sword that cuts to the right and to the left, for it exposes all faults.

Piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart: deep in its effect, reaching the depths of man's soul and spirit as the sharp sword reaches the depths of the body, so it exposes the sins of thought and heart and calls man to repentance.
The word of God is the best support for the spiritual striver in uncovering his sins, so he moves away from them and returns to God to grow in every good work.

entries.section: (3) Striving to enter the rest

paragraphs.text: St. Paul affirms that God, the Creator of all creatures, knows all that is within them because He is their Creator and Governor, and this calls us in turn to the fear of God and the rejection of sin.

entries.section: (3) Striving to enter the rest

paragraphs.text: A great high priest: Aaron the high priest was the one who entered alone into the Holy Place, but Christ, the great priest of the New Testament, is the One who enters alone into the heavens to prepare a place for us.

That is passed into the heavens: the high priest in ancient times entered with blood and passed into the Holy of Holies to make atonement for the people, and this was a type of Christ. And when he says the heavens, he means that He passed through all the heavens that mankind knows, whether the heaven of the birds or the planets or the highest heavens, to reach the heaven of heavens, that is, the Kingdom.
Profession: faith in Christ.

In our striving to reach heaven, let us hold fast to the word of God and His fear and also to faith in Christ, our High Priest and Savior, who has prepared a place for us in heaven and helps us until He brings us to it.

entries.section: (3) Striving to enter the rest

paragraphs.text: The One who encourages us to hold fast the faith, that is, our Christ, is not a God far from us, but became incarnate and endured sufferings like us to make us feel His nearness to us and His compassion for our weakness, and at the same time He is without sin, that is, able to save us from it.

entries.section: (3) Striving to enter the rest

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul urges us to boldness and confidence in approaching our great God, not only God seated on His throne, but the One who pours out His grace on us because He loved us and died for us to forgive us our sins and support us with His mercy at all times and give us His help in every affliction in which we take refuge in Him.

Trust in the love of God your Redeemer and draw near to Him however great your sins and however much afflictions increase, for He is able to rescue you because He loves you and will not leave you, so He lifts you out of your troubles and supports you on the path of your life until He brings you to Him .. trust in your victory through Him over all difficulties.
Comparison between the Levitical priesthood and the priesthood of Christ

entries.section: (1) The Jewish high priest

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul speaks about the characteristics of the Levitical priesthood, that is, Aaron and all the high priests his successors, who are taken from weak men for the service of God, and offer sacrifices on behalf of the people to obtain forgiveness of their sins from God.

entries.section: (1) The Jewish high priest

paragraphs.text: For every high priest: these are from among men and subject to human weakness, so they are able to feel and have compassion on sinners who are foolish and far away, deviating from the Law of God.

entries.section: (1) The Jewish high priest

paragraphs.text: Because the Jewish high priest is a weak man liable to sin, he offers sacrifices also for his own sins and not only for the sins of the people. This is of course unlike Christ, who does not need a sacrifice for Himself because He is righteous and holy.

entries.section: (1) The Jewish high priest

paragraphs.text: This office of high priesthood no one can take or appoint himself to, but he must have a call from God, like Aaron, who was called by name by God to this office: “Take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office” (Ex 28:1).
Christ felt our weaknesses and bore them though He is the Strong. Is it not fitting for us, being men subject to weakness like them, to feel the weaknesses of people?!

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: Likewise, the Lord Christ did not take the office of high priest from Himself, but God the Father called Him to this implicitly when the Divine inspiration revealed to us in (Ps 2:7) the depth of the relationship between God the Father and Christ the Son, which must be present in a high priest, the ability to bind his people to God.

And in the fullness of time the Father sent Him to become incarnate and redeem mankind by saying, “this day have I begotten thee”; this is a functional division within the divine Self, that the hypostasis of the Son should become incarnate to accomplish redemption. If the Jews consider Aaron a high priest because God called him, then all the more Christ is the true High Priest, whom Aaron symbolizes, because God called Him to this service as the psalm declares.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: Likewise also the calling of the Lord Christ to the priesthood, that is, His worthiness and ability to accomplish the priestly work as God incarnate, appears in (Ps 110:4), when the Father addresses the incarnate Son, “Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec” (who is a priest in the Old Testament, to be explained in detail in chapter seven), and nothing was said about his lineage or his death, so as to be a type of the eternal, everlasting priesthood of the Lord.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: This distinction of the priesthood of Christ appeared with power in the days of His being in the flesh on earth, when the Lord Christ offered, as priest and intercessor and representative of mankind, prayers and supplications with tears and intense groaning on behalf of His people, who are the whole world, knowing and feeling the weakness of mankind; so that God would accept the deliverance of the world from death in the person of the Lord Christ as priest and representative of mankind, and it appeared and was confirmed to us that He is the true High Priest who can deliver us from death in His person and by His atoning intercession for us before God, since God answered Him, because He is without sin to veil His voice and will from God, for He and God are one. His crying out in the garden of Gethsemane shows how severe were the sufferings He endured as a High Priest offering Himself as a sacrifice for the redemption of His people, and because He is righteous and without sin, the Father heard Him, that is, He was able to take away the sins of mankind and redeemed them by His death and then rose from the dead, that is, the Father raised Him, answering His cry; for the divinity raised the humanity because it is united with it even while it was in the tomb.
This verse shows the true humanity of Christ in His enduring sufferings and at the same time shows His divinity in His perfect righteousness and His resurrection from the dead.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: Learned obedience: that is, He showed obedience.

Although the Lord Christ is the Son of God and one with Him in essence, out of His love for us and His knowledge and feeling of our need, He set aside His glory and showed His submission to the will of the just God in enduring all the sufferings on behalf of mankind to the death of the Cross.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: After Christ completed redemption and then rose and ascended into heaven, everyone who believes in Him and obeys His commandments and submits to Him and receives Him by faith enjoys the eternal salvation which He Himself accomplished for us.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: By the entering of the believers into eternity the completion of Christ's work as High Priest appears, to which God the Father called Him, and He remains a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec by the glorification of His children in heaven as their Savior and Redeemer. The priesthood of Aaron was temporary, by offering sacrifices that symbolize Christ, but the priesthood of Christ is eternal after the rite and order of Melchisedec, whose explanation will come in chapter seven.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: This Melchisedec, who is a type of Christ, O Hebrews, we have much explanation concerning him, but we will not be able to speak of it now because you will not understand what will be said about him, since as a result of the hesitation and doubt that afflicted you in the faith and the desire of some of you to return to Jewish worship, your ears have become unable to understand the deeper matters.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: For the time: your knowledge about Christ from the prophecies and types of the Old Testament.
The first principles of the oracles of God: the fundamentals of faith in Christ.
Milk: the simple, easy food that is given to infants, that is, the elementary teachings of faith in Christ. Strong meat: the deep teaching about Christ.

Paul rebukes the Christians of Jewish origin for their failure to grasp the deep teaching about Christ because of their holding to the types of the Old Testament such as circumcision and their doubts about Christ. For instead of eating the strong food, that is, the deep teaching about Christ, and teaching others who are beginners, they themselves became beginners in the faith and need to have the fundamentals of the Christian faith established, and that the priesthood of Christ is what all the types of the Old Testament symbolized.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: He continues his rebuke of them in that their continuing to accept only the fundamentals of the faith hinders them from going deeper into the life of Christian righteousness and spiritual growth.

entries.section: (2) Christ the High Priest

paragraphs.text: Of full age: those who are steadfast in the faith and care about spiritual growth.
Exercised: that is, spiritual striving.
Senses: he means the inner senses, that is, spiritual understanding.

The Apostle Paul clarifies that the deep teaching about the Christian life is given to those who are steadfast in the faith and care about the salvation of their souls, in rejecting evil such as pride and doubt, for through their training in spiritual striving they easily accept what develops their relationship with God and increase in doing good, unlike the beginners who are still discussing the fundamentals of faith.

O High Priest of heaven, Jesus Christ, Son of God, who accepted all the sufferings for my sake, who stand in the Holy of Holies of heaven, have mercy on me, sick with sin, to grant me a share with You in Your Kingdom. You who bore my weakness in Yourself to turn it into strength, and took my sin to clothe me with the garment of Your righteousness, O High Priest of good things to come, I praise You because You had compassion on me. I thank You, O compassionate High Priest, who are able to have pity on my weakness; teach me to obey as You obeyed, teach me to share in Your sufferings, that this may be for me eternal salvation. Amen.
Beware of apostasy and hold fast to good works and hope

entries.section: (1) Apostasy from the faith

paragraphs.text: The principles of the doctrine of Christ: the fundamentals of the Christian life.
Perfection: spiritual growth.
Not laying again: not occupied with.
Dead works: the sins that deserve death.
Baptisms: he means the sacrament of Baptism with the details of its prayers and its kinds for infants or adults.

Laying on of hands: the laying on of the hands of the Apostles and bishops to give the Holy Spirit after Baptism (that is, the sacrament of the Holy Myron). The Apostle Paul calls the believers to leave the talk about the fundamentals of the Christian life in order to advance in spiritual growth, and these fundamentals are:
1- Repentance and faith, which represent the basis of man's readiness to enter Christianity.
2- Baptism and the Holy Myron, which are the first two sacraments that God gives to those coming to Christianity.

3- The resurrection and judgment, which are the hope of those who have begun the Christian life, that is, the resurrection of their bodies on the last day and passing the last judgment to enter the Kingdom.

All these fundamentals he has finished speaking about, and they need to be occupied with spiritual growth. This is what the Apostle indicates is the most important and will do, that is, he will speak about how to grow spiritually in order to enjoy fellowship with God.

entries.section: (1) Apostasy from the faith

paragraphs.text: Once enlightened: they received the sacrament of Baptism.
The heavenly gift: the sacrament of the Holy Myron, that is, the descent of the Holy Spirit.
The powers of the world to come: they performed miracles and experienced God in their lives with deep spiritual feelings, which are a glimmer of the light of eternity.
Fall away: apostatize from the Christian faith.
To renew them: it is not possible to repeat their baptism if they repent and return to the faith.

They crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame: the baptized person dies with Christ by being buried in the water of Baptism and then rises with Him, so the one who is baptized receives the power of Christ's crucifixion, death and resurrection, and this happens once, and Christ cannot be crucified twice for the baptized man, so if Baptism were repeated it would be as though we crucify Christ another time and put Him to shame, that is, clothe Him with disgrace after He rose from the dead.

In these verses the Apostle Paul answers a question concerning those who have apostatized from the faith, after receiving the sacrament of Baptism and the Myron and the gifts of the Holy Spirit and enjoying the word of God and even performing miracles and experiencing the work of God in them: is their baptism to be repeated? He says that their baptism cannot be repeated because renewal means Baptism and not repentance in the sacrament of confession, and renewal happens once because it is a death and resurrection with Christ, who died and rose once, so this happens in man once and he receives a new nature; and if it is soiled by sin, even if it be apostasy from the faith, it is healed by repentance and confession. This view is the view of St. John Chrysostom.

And there are views of other Fathers such as Tertullian, which is that these verses mean the Jews who became Christians and then returned to their Jewish life and insist on not returning to Christianity, or everyone who insists on his sins and does not want to repent and return to Christ; they interpret the word fall away as meaning persistence and continuance in sin throughout life, and accordingly their not being renewed and receiving forgiveness in the sacrament of confession is due to their own refusal and not God's rejection of them, and by their sins they crucify Christ a second time and clothe Him with disgrace and shame by their refusal to repent.

entries.section: (1) Apostasy from the faith

paragraphs.text: He likens the spiritual man who is steadfast in the faith to land on which rain falls, that is, God's blessings through spiritual teachings and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, so it yields good plants, that is, fruits of the Holy Spirit which the believers enjoy and God rejoices in them and gives them the glories of the Kingdom.

entries.section: (1) Apostasy from the faith

paragraphs.text: He completes the comparison and says that if this land does not produce good fruits after receiving abundant rains, meaning those who believed and lived with Christ for a time and then apostatized and fell into various sins, they are rejected by God and near to destruction, and the solution is their repentance and return to the faith from which they apostatized, so that God forgives them and they regain their membership in the Church.

May you benefit from God's continual blessings to you which you receive from the Church in the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace, and not take them superficially so that their work in you is lost; and the sacrament of repentance restores your spiritual zeal so that you become active anew and deepen your relationship with God.

entries.section: (2) Encouragement to good works

paragraphs.text: The Apostle qualifies his words and encourages the Christians of Jewish origin with his confidence that they enjoy the Christian life and the blessings of salvation in the Church, and that by his previous words he meant a warning against apostasy from Christ, and if one of them falls, his repentance can be accepted in the sacrament of confession. He is concerned to encourage them so that they do not fall into faintheartedness or despair because of their weaknesses.

entries.section: (2) Encouragement to good works

paragraphs.text: For God is not unrighteous to forget the good works and their sincere love which they showed in labors for the sake of His name, to Him be glory, since they did not stop serving the believers and continue in that to this time.

entries.section: (2) Encouragement to good works

paragraphs.text: Some Christians showed their concern for serving those in need, so Paul wishes that all the believers would care about these services, and he encourages them to continue and care about good works throughout their lives, for they are the proof of their faith and their hope in God.

entries.section: (2) Encouragement to good works

paragraphs.text: He continues to encourage them to reject laziness and to imitate the holy fathers, such as Abraham, in holding fast to the faith, patience in hardships and continuing the striving until they obtain God's promises and inherit the Kingdom.

Take care to encourage others, for it is in most cases more acceptable and effective with people than reproach and rebuke. Rebuke and punishment are important at times, but because of suffering from many afflictions, which sometimes lead to negligence and laziness, people need to regain their confidence in themselves and in God's love through your kind words. And this encouragement gives you too zeal and hope.

entries.section: (3) Hope in God's promises

paragraphs.text: God wanted to confirm His promise to Abraham with an oath as people are accustomed to confirm their words, and since He found no one greater than Himself to swear by, He swore by Himself to confirm the truth of what He promises.

entries.section: (3) Hope in God's promises

paragraphs.text: God promised Abraham many blessings and descendants too many to be counted.

entries.section: (3) Hope in God's promises

paragraphs.text: Abraham believed and was patient in enduring sufferings and lived a righteous life, so he obtained God's promises when Isaac was born while he was a hundred years old and Sarah ninety, and this was a prelude to God's blessings which Abraham would receive in heaven.

entries.section: (3) Hope in God's promises

paragraphs.text: For it is the custom of people, when affirming facts to their hearers in case of any dispute between them, to swear by the greatest they know in order to confirm their agreement and covenants. And God permitted swearing by His name in the Old Testament to declare that He is the one God and not the gods of the pagan Gentiles, but in the New Testament He forbade it because there was no need for it after faith in Him had become established.

entries.section: (3) Hope in God's promises

paragraphs.text: Therefore when God wanted to confirm His promise to Abraham and to his children, who are we the believers, He used an oath.

entries.section: (3) Hope in God's promises

paragraphs.text: In order that God might gladden us and establish our hope in Him, He confirmed the truth of His word by two things, which are:
1- His promise of blessing.
2- The oath.

entries.section: (3) Hope in God's promises

paragraphs.text: An anchor: the anchor that is cast into the sea to fix in its bottom and hold the ship so that the waves do not carry it away from the shore, and it is a symbol of the hope that establishes the spiritual man in life with God. The veil: the curtain that separates between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies and which only the high priest passes through, once every year, with blood to make atonement with it before the ark of the covenant that is in the Holy of Holies. And passing through the veil signifies Christ's passing through and His ascension into the heavens as High Priest to intercede for us and prepare a place for us there.

The Apostle likens hope to an anchor that establishes the spiritual man in the love of eternity, which Christ prepared for us and passed into as our representative by His ascension after His resurrection, and He remains there interceding for us forever because He is a priest after the order of Melchisedec, that is, the eternal priesthood, and not the temporary, symbolic priesthood of Aaron in which bloody sacrifices are used.

Look to the hope of eternal life and God's promises to you so that you are encouraged however afflictions surround you, for they are temporary, and trust in the love of God, who turns afflictions into blessings and gives you in place of them glories in heaven.
Christ and Melchisedec

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: For this Melchisedec, the great one, king of Jerusalem, whose name was formerly Salem, that is, peace or king of peace, was in the days of the first fathers a priest of the Most High God; this priest and king met our father Abraham, the father of fathers and greatly honored among the Hebrews, when he was returning victorious over the four kings who took Lot captive, and the Old Testament mentions that this Melchisedec blessed the father of fathers Abraham (Gen 14).

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: Abraham felt the greatness of Melchisedec, so he gave him a tenth of the spoils he obtained from his victory over the four kings, and the giving of the tithe was a sign of his priesthood, and Abraham asked for the blessing from Melchisedec. The meaning of the name Melchisedec in the Arabic language is king of righteousness, and also king of Salem in the Hebrew language: that is, king of peace.

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: This Melchisedec appeared suddenly in the Divine inspiration without any mention of who his father or mother was or his lineage in order to prove the validity of his priesthood, since in the Aaronic priesthood it was necessary to be sure of the validity of a person's descent from Aaron so as to be accepted as a Jewish priest (Ezra 2:62). And the Old Testament did not mention the beginning of Melchisedec's life or its end because he is likened to our Lord Jesus Christ, who has no father in the flesh and has neither beginning nor end, for He is eternal and everlasting, and because our Lord Jesus Christ is the Son of God He remains a priest forever.

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: Consider, O Hebrew brethren, how great this Melchisedec was, for our father Abraham, the chief of the first fathers, the one of the divine calling, from whom came the whole Hebrew people, gave him a tenth of the spoils he had, which is a sign of Abraham's submission to Melchisedec by asking the blessing from him.

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: While Abraham gave tithes to Melchisedec like this, without any command mentioned beforehand concerning Melchisedec, we find that the priests of the tribe of Levi, who have the right of the priesthood in the Old Testament in Israel, take tithes from their brethren, with less honor, by a commandment of the Law, and not as Abraham gave Melchisedec tithes of his own accord as a sign of submission and a request for blessing.

And we notice that all the tribes give tithes to the tribe of Levi although these tribes have the honor of Abraham because they are his descendants, but the commandment orders them to give tithes to the tribe of Levi, which like them is from the descendants of Abraham. So it appears from this that the honor of the tribe of Levi is less than the honor of Melchisedec, although both take tithes.

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: Melchisedec, whose lineage is not known, blessed Abraham, who received the promises from God, and took tithes from him, and from him came the tribe of Levi, which takes tithes from its brethren, that is, the rest of the tribes.

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: Without all contradiction: certainly and without dispute.
There is no doubt that he who gives the blessing is greater than he who receives the blessing, that is, Melchisedec was more honored than Abraham.

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: Mortal: their lives end in death.

The priests of the tribe of Levi who take tithes end their lives in death, but Christ the High Priest lives forever in the likeness of Melchisedec, who took the tenth from Abraham, because Melchisedec is a type of Christ; Christ is living, whereas the Levitical priesthood is merely a symbol of Him because the priests of the Old Testament die.

entries.section: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

paragraphs.text: So that I say to you a word that settles the comparison between the Levitical priesthood, to which some of you may try to hold fast, and the priesthood of the Lord Christ, which is after the order of the priesthood of Melchisedec: that Levi, who took tithes from the people in the person of Aaron the priest, paid tithes to Melchisedec, a sign of honor, because he was still in the loins of his father Abraham, who represents the whole Hebrew people, since from his descendants, that is, from the descendants of Abraham, all the tribes of the people came forth, including the tribe of Levi.

If you are humble you can receive God's blessings from many people and see their virtues and learn from them, and since God sees your humility He gives you many graces beyond what you ask, so learn from everyone, even children.

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ
