paragraphs.text: If the perfection of salvation was through the Levitical priesthood, when the people of the children of Israel received at its hands the Mosaic Law and the legislation of the Old Testament, why did the psalms prophesy of the coming of another priest after the order of Melchisedec and not after the order of Levi, that is, the priesthood of Aaron: “The LORD sware, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek” (Ps 110:4).

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: Since the priesthood has among its tasks conveying the message of the Law from God to the people, the mention in the psalm of the change of the priesthood from the tribe of Levi to the priesthood of Melchisedec is a decisive proof of the need to change the Law needed for the salvation that God wants to teach the people, so that it changes from the Law that was given at the hand of the Levitical priesthood, a law that gave perfection to no one, to the law of the grace of Christ Jesus, who came after the order of Melchisedec, fulfilling the prophecy that came about Him in (Ps 110:4).

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: He of whom these things are spoken: he means Christ.

Because the One spoken of in this prophecy, our Lord Jesus Christ, was of a tribe from which no one served as priest or attended at the altar, for it is known to everyone that our Lord Jesus Christ came from the tribe of Judah, of which Moses gave no commandment to perform the priestly work.

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: Confirming that the Law must be changed, the psalm made clear that another priest in the likeness of Melchisedec would come afterward, and he is Christ.

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: The priesthood of the Lord Christ, which is after the order of this Melchisedec, was not for us to give us an external, fleshly commandment that does not affect our souls or change them, but it is a priesthood that gave us the power of righteousness and the grace of inner change and an everlasting life that does not pass away.

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: The psalm (Ps 110:4) testifies that the Lord Christ will be a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec, that is, as Melchisedec offered in his priesthood an offering of bread and wine and did not offer an animal sacrifice, so also the Lord Christ offered a bodily sacrifice under the appearance (form) of bread and wine (Mt 26:26-27).

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: By Christ the usefulness of the Law was ended and the shortcoming of what the Levitical priesthood offered appeared, for it gave us only an external commandment that exposes sin but does not give power to be rid of it, and a commandment that urges to righteousness but without giving us the ability to practice it.

entries.section: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: Because the Law did not complete our salvation, we necessarily needed another salvation, and this was accomplished by Christ, who gives us hope, a hope by which we can draw near to God, unlike the people in the Old Testament, who had to stand far off, unable to approach God or the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

Do not reject any new idea because you have become accustomed to another thought, but examine it with care, for it may be the more correct, and prayer with the guidance of guides supports you to know what is better.

entries.section: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: The first reason for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ is that God confirmed it with an oath, but those priests of the Levitical order became priests without a word of oath, because they were merely a type of the One typified, the Lord Christ, to Him be glory, the true Priest, the One of whom God assured us with an oath in the Divine inspiration in the psalm, saying that God swore and will not at all go back on His word that you (Christ) shall remain a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec (Ps 110:4).

entries.section: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: By the greatness of the divine oath Christ became as a representative of mankind and a priest for ourselves who guarantees us a new and better covenant with its spiritual promises and the work of God's rich grace in our lives.

entries.section: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: The second reason for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ is the weakness of the priests of the Old Testament, because they are men who die, so there were accordingly many of them, one to take the place of another.

entries.section: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: But our Lord Jesus Christ, because He is God manifest in the flesh and living forever, is distinguished and different from the human, mortal priests of the tribe of Levi in His remaining forever, and as a result His priesthood does not pass away or end, because the person of Christ, to Him be glory, does not die.

entries.section: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: That come unto God by him: they take shelter in His blood that atones for them.

On this account, and because of the remaining of Christ, to Him be glory, living forever, He is able to save to the uttermost, that is, even after our death and our standing before God in eternal life; we also find Him supporting us after our death, interceding for us before the Father as a priest who feels our weaknesses, and we take shelter in Him before the fearful and just God; this is because He lives at all times above the ages.

And here we notice that the priestly ministry of the Aaronic high priest stops at his death, whereas our Lord Jesus Christ began by His death, as a sacrifice for the sins of the world, His priestly ministry, which lasts forever.

entries.section: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: The third reason for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ is His holiness and His innocence of every sin; He who, as proof of His righteousness, has been lifted above sharing in the deeds of our sinful world, glorified with great honor, and was able to enter the Holy of Holies of heaven without offering a sacrifice for Himself like the high priests of the Levitical priesthood, who are always compelled, in making atonement for the sins of the people, to offer several sacrifices and not one sacrifice; they offer sacrifices first for themselves because they are sinners like the rest of the people for whom they offer the sacrifices. But Christ does not need a sacrifice because He is without sin, but He offered Himself as an atoning sacrifice for the whole world once, because in His redeeming work is the perfection of salvation, so it does not need to be repeated by Him.

entries.section: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

paragraphs.text: For the Law of the Old Testament set up for us men weak people as high priests only in symbol, who cannot offer us complete salvation, but the word of God in His oath, which was made clear to us in the psalm that came after the Law, revealed to us the person of our Lord Jesus Christ, the true Priest, who completed for us and for our sake this eternal salvation. And this is proof of the insufficiency of what came in the Law for our salvation, we men.

If Christ has offered us a great salvation like this, let us hold fast to Him by our attachment to the Church and distance from every sin, and as much as we thank Him, we live in His righteousness, caring about every good work. Christ gives us heaven and the blessings of the New Testament. St. Paul continues in this chapter to draw a comparison between the earthly Hebrew high priest from the tribe of Levi and the Lord Christ, and here he brings out the distinction of the Lord Christ, to Him be glory, for in His priestly work He is able to enter the Holy of Holies of heaven itself, not the Holy of Holies of an earthly tabernacle made by men as a model which God gave to man of the true, heavenly tabernacle in which God dwells.

entries.section: (1) Christ the heavenly priest

paragraphs.text: Of the things which we have spoken, this is the sum: that is, the summary of the discourse.
Sat down: that is, settled, and it means His permanence in glory.
Right hand: glory and power.
Throne: the supreme honor.

He concludes from the comparisons in the previous chapters between Christ on the one hand and the angels, Moses, Joshua and Aaron on the other, that as High Priest He has accomplished our redemption on the Cross and ascended into the heavens to His first glory to remain in it forever, interceding for us and waiting for us to be glorified with Him.

entries.section: (1) Christ the heavenly priest

paragraphs.text: A minister: a High Priest who intercedes for us by His blood forever.

Of the sanctuary: the heavenly throne of God, which the Holy of Holies in the tabernacle of the congregation symbolized. The true tabernacle: the heavens, which the tabernacle of the congregation symbolized and which is called the dwelling, that is, God's dwelling in the midst of His people.

Christ ascended after accomplishing our redemption to intercede for us in the heavens which God Himself created and prepared, and not in the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon which men made.

entries.section: (1) Christ the heavenly priest

paragraphs.text: The Levitical high priest must offer bloody sacrifices to make atonement for himself and his people before God, and these symbolize Christ; accordingly Christ, our High Priest, offered the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross for our redemption and presents it to us every day on the altar as true Body and Blood.

entries.section: (1) Christ the heavenly priest

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul affirms that Christ is the heavenly Priest whom we await to give us salvation and eternal life, because if He had remained on earth and had not died and redeemed us, He would have been like the priests of the tribe of Levi who offer bloody sacrifices that symbolize the coming Priest who raises us to the heavens.

entries.section: (1) Christ the heavenly priest

paragraphs.text: The Jewish high priests did not serve the heavenly things themselves like the Lord Christ, but the example and shadow of heavenly things, and this is clear in the Book of Exodus (Ex 25:40) from God's words to Moses to take care to make the tabernacle of the congregation and everything in it according to the pattern that He showed him while he was with Him on Mount Sinai, as a confirmation from St. Paul that what they serve is an example and a symbol.

entries.section: (1) Christ the heavenly priest

paragraphs.text: A more excellent ministry: the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross in place of animal sacrifices.
A better covenant: the covenant of grace that supports man in carrying out the commandment, and not the covenant of the Law that judges man's weakness and shortcoming.
Better promises: the inheritance of the Kingdom of Heaven and not the inheritance of the Promised Land, that is, earthly Canaan.

St. Paul summarizes the redeeming work of Christ as a ministry better than the ministry of the priesthood of the Old Testament, which consisted of bloody sacrifices, and by His redemption of us on the Cross the covenant of grace began, in which He supports us to carry out His commandments so that we receive the greatest promises, which are the Kingdom of Heaven.

Lift me up, beloved, my Lord Jesus Christ, from the superficiality of earthly things to the depth of the spiritual things of heaven; pick me up, the wretched one, from the dunghill and seat me by Your favor and Your grace with the nobles of Your children in heaven; turn my eyes so that I do not see or look at or care about the vanities of the earth, but truly enjoy seeing You in those around me. O High Priest of heaven, You alone have all power to lift me to heaven; help my weakness and free me from the thoughts of dust to the glory of heaven; put to death my earthly senses, my God, and awaken my spiritual senses; You know and I know my weakness, but I have complete confidence, my God Jesus Christ, in the power of Your work and in the power of Your love. Amen.

entries.section: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

paragraphs.text: For if the first covenant, which preceded the Lord Christ, with its laws and the work of the earthly high priests, had given righteousness to mankind and saved them from their sins, God would not have spoken in the Book of Jeremiah about the need for another covenant (Jer 31:31-34).

entries.section: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul continues God's words in Jeremiah mentioned in (Jer 31), clarifying that God rebukes them for their many sins and their division into two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, and at the same time encourages them with hope in the New Testament which He makes with them by His redemption of them on the Cross, and it is higher than the Old Testament with its bloody sacrifices that symbolize Christ.

entries.section: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

paragraphs.text: The New Testament, which is by the blood of Christ the Redeemer, is not like the first covenant that He made in the days of their exodus from Egypt by the hand of Moses by the slaying of the Passover lamb, and He warned them against turning back from it when He said, “Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the LORD your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the LORD thy God hath forbidden thee” (Deut 4:23). But after He freed them from the bondage of Egypt they betrayed the covenant and worshipped the golden calf (Ex 32:8), so God was angry with them and abandoned them partially so that they might repent.

entries.section: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

paragraphs.text: The Apostle completes God's words in Jeremiah about His covenant with His people Israel who believe in Christ the Redeemer; in this New Testament God renews their hearts, so they believe His commandments and hold fast to them with their hearts and their thoughts, and not merely a literal application of them but they remain steadfast in them, and a covenant of reconciliation with Him begins, so that His being their God is a source of joy and delight and rest for them, and they boast that He is their God, and He rejoices in them as His own people brought near to Him.

entries.section: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

paragraphs.text: God continues His speech in Jeremiah, and tells them of the work of His Holy Spirit in those who believe in Him in the New Testament, where the Holy Spirit dwells in every believer and makes him know God and binds him to Him in the holy Church, so that God is made known to all His children who believe in Him in the whole world, and is not known to one people, the Jews, or to the prophets only, but the Holy Spirit works in all, the great and the small, the deep and the simple, the advanced and the beginners.

And this is of course not against spiritual discipleship and learning in the Church from the Holy Spirit, because the Spirit is one and He is the One who works in every person and in the Church as a whole.

entries.section: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah adds that God forgives the sins of His people who believe in Him in the New Testament by the blood of Christ the Redeemer, and this is accomplished in the sacraments of Baptism, confession and Communion.

entries.section: (2) The blessings of the New Testament

paragraphs.text: The New Testament which Christ the Redeemer made has made the covenant of symbolic sacrifices old, since it symbolized the New Testament, and the old symbolic passes away with the coming of the new, just as any man who grows old in days is near to death or any material that has existed a long time is old and liable to perish and decay. So he declares clearly to the Christians of Jewish origin the necessity of holding fast to the Christian faith and leaving aside all the legal customs which became worthless after the coming of Christ.

May you enjoy the grace of the New Testament through the Holy Sacraments to receive forgiveness of your sins and strength for spiritual growth and enjoyment of God's commandments. Care about prayers and meditations to receive an abundance of God's grace.
The sacrifices are a symbol of the blood of Christ. In this chapter St. Paul clarifies the atoning work of Christ in cleansing us from our sins, which the bloody sacrifices are unable to do.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: The first covenant which God made with Moses for the people of Israel, by the making of the tabernacle of the congregation for Him to dwell in among them, set for it regulations for worship and the offering of sacrifices. And the tabernacle had an earthly sanctuary that symbolizes the heavenly dwelling.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: The first tabernacle: it is called the Holy Place, and only the priests enter it, and a curtain separates it from the Holy of Holies. The candlestick: a lampstand with seven lamps, that is, wicks, in round holders shaped like an almond flower, lit with olive oil, and it symbolizes the Holy Spirit and is on the left of one entering the Holy Place. The table: its length 90 cm, its width 45 cm and its height about 68 cm, made of acacia wood, which is a strong wood, and overlaid with gold, and it is on the right of one entering the Holy Place. The shewbread: also called the bread of the Presence, placed on the aforementioned table, always twelve loaves, which are before the face of the Lord from Sabbath to Sabbath, and the priests eat it on the Sabbath day so that new bread may be put.
The Holy Place contains the candlestick and the table of the shewbread in addition to the altar of incense which is in the middle and will be referred to in the following verses.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: At the entrance of the Holy Place there was a veil, which is the first veil that separates the Holy Place from the outer court, as shown in figure (1), and then another veil (the second veil) screens the Holy Place from the area in which the ark of the covenant is; and this area beyond the second veil was called the Holy of Holies because the Lord used to appear in it between the cherubim in the form of a cloud.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: A golden censer in which he takes incense from the altar of incense that is in the Holy Place and enters with it into the Holy of Holies to offer incense before the ark of the covenant.
The ark of the covenant: a chest 112.5 cm long, 67.5 cm wide and 67.5 cm high, made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold, with the two cherubim above it.
The golden pot: a vessel of gold in which a portion of the manna was placed.
The manna: food that God gave His people every day in the wilderness, and it symbolizes Christ our true food.

Aaron's rod: Moses put the rods of the tribes of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of the congregation, and Aaron's rod budded and brought forth blossoms and fruit, confirming God's choice of him as priest and not all Israel (Num 17:8). The tables of the covenant: two tablets of stone which Moses received from God on the mountain, on which the Ten Commandments were written.

The Holy of Holies has in it the ark of the covenant, and inside the ark are the tables of the covenant, the pot of manna and Aaron's rod. And the high priest enters with a censer into the Holy of Holies once every year to burn incense before the ark. (Figures 2, 3).

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: The cherubims of glory: two statues of two angels of the order of the Cherubim, that is, the Cherubim, an angelic order that symbolizes divine justice, and these two angels are fixed on the cover of the ark and overshadow it with their wings (figure 2).

The mercyseat: it is the cover of the ark and is called the mercy seat, on which the high priest sprinkles the blood, so that divine justice, which the Cherubim symbolize, sees it, and God forgives the sins of the people; it is a symbol of the blood of Christ, who saved us by His mercy and satisfied divine justice.

After Paul has mentioned briefly what is inside the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, he declares that these are symbols of the sacrifice of Christ, and does not want to enter into the details of their making and their spiritual meanings because he wants to concentrate on the One symbolized, the sacrifice of Christ.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: The first tabernacle: the Holy Place.

After Moses set up the tabernacle in the order that God declared to him on the mountain, the priests used to enter every day. And here St. Paul intends to point out that the service which the priests performed was not sufficient, therefore it was offered repeatedly, that is, at all times, in the Holy Place only, as evidence of the absence of reconciliation between God and mankind owing to the absence of a sacrifice able to atone for the sin that screens between God and mankind; so the bloody sacrifices were offered before the Holy Place on the altar of burnt offering every day until Christ came, who offers the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross and enters the higher holies, that is, heaven, and makes atonement for us.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: Concerning the Holy of Holies, which is the second tabernacle, only the high priest used to enter it, once a year on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16:2, Ex 30:10), and when Aaron the high priest enters the Holy of Holies he needs to offer a sacrifice for himself and for the people, because he is not perfect as a high priest from sinful men, for he needs to make atonement for his sins and ignorances along with the ignorances of the people. And this sacrifice symbolized Christ.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: By the existence of the Holy Place, that is, the first tabernacle, and the veil, God declares that the way to the Holy of Holies was still not open and that the reconciliation between God and people and the occurrence of true atonement had not yet happened, because there is a barrier between God and mankind which the Holy Place and the second veil symbolize. This veil, we must not fail to mention, was rent at the time of the Cross at the death of the Lord Christ, to declare by this that the way to heaven became open through the perfection of the atonement that was accomplished on the wood of the Cross by the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and this is what St. Paul will confirm in the coming verses of this chapter.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: Which: the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon.
The time then present: the New Testament, that is, after the completion of redemption.

Could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience: they do not cleanse and forgive the sins of the priest and the people. The gifts and sacrifices that are offered in the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon cannot cleanse the one who offers them.

entries.section: (1) The tabernacle of the congregation

paragraphs.text: The time of reformation: the redemption on the Cross.

The Jewish sacrifices and offerings consisted of meats and drinks and many washings and external ordinances practiced only as symbols until the time when the true sacrifice would come, that is, the Lord Christ, who has the power to renew and reform the nature of man.

As long as the way is open before you to reach God through Christ the Redeemer, hasten to prayer with the boldness of sonship and enjoy being in His hands at all times, and as much as you are able unite with Him by receiving His Body and Blood, and you will rejoice with inexpressible joy.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: Of good things to come: the eternal glories.
A greater and more perfect tabernacle: the Kingdom of Heaven.

The Jewish high priest used to enter the Holy of Holies in which the ark of the covenant was, but Christ, the true High Priest, who gives us the glories of eternity and whom the Jewish high priests symbolize, brings us into the Kingdom of Heaven which God made and not the hands of men.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: The holy place: the Kingdom of Heaven.

Christ did not need bloody sacrifices, but by His death on the Cross He offered Himself as a sacrifice once and accomplished redemption and entered by it into the Kingdom of Heaven to declare the possibility of the entering of those who believe in Him into this place.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: Goats: male goats.

The ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean: among the rites of the Jews was to slay a red cow and burn it before God and then put water on its ashes with which the one who becomes unclean is sprinkled to be cleansed (Num 19). Paul declares that the blood of animal sacrifices of bulls and goats and the remains of the burning of the red cow cleanse the bodies of those made unclean by touching a dead person or anything unclean.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: Through the eternal Spirit: the Holy Spirit.
Dead works: the sins that lead to eternal death.

If the bloody sacrifices cleanse the body, how much more the blood of Christ, who is without sin and offered it for us before the Father, cleanses not only our bodies but our spirits from all sins and their consequences, which are eternal death, and gives us new life in Him, so that we even serve Him forever.

If Christ has cleansed us by His redemption and rescued us from the authority of sin and death that we may live for Him, we ought to be occupied with His love and the acquisition of virtues and striving to serve all those around us, for this is our only purpose for existence.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: They which are called: those who believe in Christ.
The transgressions that were under the first testament: the sins that the Old Testament was unable to forgive by the bloody sacrifices.

Because of the inability of animal sacrifices to forgive the sins of mankind, Christ came forward with His blood to be the mediator of the New Testament by His death on the Cross, so He gives salvation to everyone who believes in Him to receive eternal life.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: A testament takes its force in the case of the death of the one who made it according to civil law, but if he has not died the testament is not carried out.

And the testator is God, and the testament is His promise of salvation which He gave in the Old Testament to the fathers, and these promises are not fulfilled except by the death of Christ, that is, God incarnate, so we receive salvation and eternal life.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: The first: the prophet Moses.

For the necessity of Christ's death in order to redeem us, he declares that the consecration and sanctification of everything in the Old Testament was by the death of the sacrifices and the shedding of their blood, so the prophet Moses was sanctified by the shedding of the blood of animal sacrifices, and they symbolize Christ, who by His blood sanctifies us.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: Scarlet: the dark red color.
Hyssop: plant branches with leaves that are held as a bunch and dipped in the blood and used to sprinkle things. The book: which contains the Law of the Lord.
After Moses commanded the people with all the teachings of the Law he slew sacrifices and sprinkled some of their blood with the wool and hyssop on the book of the Law and on the people (Ex 24:8).

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: Moses declared at the sprinkling of the blood that by it the covenant between them and God is established, for the covenant is not accomplished without blood.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: Moses completed the sanctification of the tabernacle of the congregation and all the vessels and instruments of the service in it by sprinkling the blood on them.

entries.section: (2) The blood of Christ and the blood of the sacrifices

paragraphs.text: We notice in the rites of the Old Testament that most of the cleansing is done by the sprinkling of blood, and by this the sins of the people are forgiven, for blood is necessary for the forgiveness of sin.

entries.section: (3) The ascension of Christ and His second coming

paragraphs.text: The patterns of things in the heavens: the tabernacle of the congregation and its contents.
With these: the animal sacrifices.
The heavenly things themselves: the souls of the believers in which God dwells, so that they become a heaven on earth and dwell in heaven forever.

With better sacrifices: the sacrifice of Christ, in which all the types of the Mosaic sacrifices are gathered. If the tabernacle of the congregation and all that is in it are cleansed by sprinkling the blood of animals on them, this symbolizes the Church and the believers, who become a heaven in which God dwells, so that they are cleansed by a sacrifice better than the animal sacrifices, which is the blood of Christ.

entries.section: (3) The ascension of Christ and His second coming

paragraphs.text: Christ did not enter the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies which are in the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon, but by His ascension He entered into heaven and presented His blood as redemption for us before God, and He continues to intercede for us by His blood forever.

entries.section: (3) The ascension of Christ and His second coming

paragraphs.text: The high priest on the Day of Atonement used to enter with blood which he sprinkled in the Holy of Holies on the ark of the covenant, and this happens once every year (Lev 16:29, 30), but the sacrifice of Christ is unlimited, atoning for all sins, therefore He offered Himself once on the Cross and entered by this redemption into heaven to satisfy divine justice and to prepare a place for us.

entries.section: (3) The ascension of Christ and His second coming

paragraphs.text: If the sacrifice of the Lord Christ were insufficient for salvation like the sacrifice of atonement, it would have to resemble it in its repetition, that is, in its weakness, so He would suffer and be crucified and die many times since the foundation of the world and with the repetition of men's sins; but in the last days in which we live, He appeared once to die and to take away from us the authority of sin and death, since His sacrifice is unlimited, so it cleanses all the sins of the people who believe in Him.

entries.section: (3) The ascension of Christ and His second coming

paragraphs.text: As God appointed for every man to die once as a result of his sins and then be judged on the last day, so also Christ died as a representative of mankind once to redeem us and save us from our sins and the authority of death, and then He appears on the Day of Judgment to intercede for us by His blood and save us from eternal death and bring us with Him into the Kingdom of Heaven.

Christ ascended to prepare a place for us, so may we think of the beauty of eternity so that we give God sufficient time and taste fellowship with Him in prayers and meditations, and then we keep away from sin, which is not fitting for the heavenly ones. Figure (1) The ark of the covenant. Figure (2) (The bronze altar). Figure (3) Abiding in Christ.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: The Law and all the worship of the Old Testament signify the grace of God in the Church of the New Testament, which we receive in the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace. Consequently, the Law cannot, by animal sacrifices, cleanse and justify those who offer them.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: "Should have had no more conscience of sins": they would no longer fear the punishment of sin.

The blood sacrifices offered by the priests and the Levites were for cleansing their hearts from every sin, and they had to be repeated; once was not enough, because they are a type of the complete cleansing by the blood of Christ.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: He draws them on by saying that the sacrifices are repeated every year, which is proof of their inability to cleanse hearts from sin. The blood of animals is unable to cleanse men from their sins; it is merely a symbol.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: David the prophet speaks in the spirit of prophecy in (Ps 40:6) about Christ at His incarnation and His coming into the world. The Son says to the Father that You do not desire animal sacrifices, for they are merely a symbol, but You desire the sacrifice of my body, which I offer on the Cross; therefore You have prepared me a body by my birth from the Virgin.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: "The volume of the book": the ancient books were written on parchments and rolled up, and were called a volume. By "the book" is meant the books of the Old Testament, which prophesied of the coming of Christ.
Christ, the incarnate One of whom the prophecies spoke, would become incarnate in the fullness of time to do the will of God, which is redemption on the Cross.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: "Above": previously.
As the Psalm (40:6) mentioned previously that God had no pleasure in animal sacrifices, so Paul warns the Hebrews that these sacrifices are merely symbols, so that they would not cling to them.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: Since God has no pleasure in animal sacrifices but in the sacrifice of Christ, God by this takes away the symbolic animal sacrifices and establishes the sacrifice of Christ, in which the Hebrews must believe, and they must leave behind the old sacrifices.

entries.section: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

paragraphs.text: St. Paul the Apostle declares in conclusion that sanctification is accomplished by the will of God, which He fulfilled in the crucifixion of Christ and His redemption of us.

We thank God, who has granted us, by partaking of His Body and Blood, forgiveness of our sins and strength to live with Him. May we partake often, as much as we feel our weakness, our need and our love for Him.

entries.section: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

paragraphs.text: Every Jewish priest stood daily for the priestly service in the Old Testament and offered again the same sacrifices, which were utterly unable to cleanse and to take away sin.

entries.section: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

paragraphs.text: "Sat down on the right hand of God": He showed the permanence of His power and His divine glory.

The Lord Christ, after He was crucified and offered one sacrifice for the sins of the whole world as an atonement for sins, declared by His ascension His power and glory, by which He saves His children continually.

entries.section: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

paragraphs.text: Christ continues to support His children and to rescue them from the wars of the devil, until at the end He brings them into the Kingdom of Heaven and tramples all the power of the devil when He casts him into eternal torment.

entries.section: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

paragraphs.text: By the sacrifice of Christ, which is signified by the offerings and sacrifices of the Old Testament, this one sacrifice or offering gives complete salvation to those who believe in Him.

entries.section: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

paragraphs.text: The Holy Spirit prophesied beforehand through Jeremiah (Jer 31:32, 33) that after the passing of the Old Testament, and the incarnation of Christ and His redemption, He would establish His word and His commandments in the minds and hearts of those who believe in Him, and this by the work of the Holy Spirit in them and in the Church and through the Holy Sacraments.

entries.section: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

paragraphs.text: God forgives the sins of His people through the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion, so that they are completely blotted out from them.

entries.section: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

paragraphs.text: After the believers enjoy forgiveness in the Church, they have no need to offer the sacrifices and offerings of the Old Testament.

Ask in prayer for the help of the Holy Spirit when you read the words of the Holy Bible, that He may give you understanding of them and make you moved by them, and establish them within you, so that you apply them and live by them, and rejoice in His work in you.

entries.section: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

paragraphs.text: In sum, beloved brethren, because we now have boldness to enter into heaven itself by the blood of Christ. He said Jesus alone, without Christ, because He wishes here to stress that He is a representative of men as the Son of Man, to declare the possibility of the redeemed entering heaven by His redemption of us.

entries.section: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

paragraphs.text: "The veil": the curtain between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, which was a type of Christ. When He was crucified and His body was rent, that is, when He died on the Cross, the veil of the Temple was rent, declaring the completion of salvation and the possibility of man's entering heaven, that is, the highest Holy of Holies, and the possibility of our partaking of His Body and Blood in the Church as a pledge of the Kingdom.

By the redemption of Christ, which He recently accomplished on the Cross, He prepared for us the way of the Kingdom, and His body, which He gave on the Cross, He offers to us on the altar every day as a pledge of the Kingdom that He has prepared for us.

entries.section: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

paragraphs.text: We also have a greater priest, perfect, holy and without evil, who is Christ, over the house of God, which is the Church and heaven also.

entries.section: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

paragraphs.text: He calls us to spiritual growth with pure and sincere hearts, steadfast in faith in Christ the Redeemer, to whom all the sacrifices of the Old Testament point, and that our consciences may be purified by His blood shed for us through the sacrament of repentance and confession, and our bodies washed with the water of Baptism, so that our nature is renewed and we live for Him. This is in place of the sprinkling of the blood of sacrifices to cleanse the defiled and sinners, or their washing with water for cleansing in the Old Testament.

entries.section: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

paragraphs.text: "The profession of our hope unwavering": we declare and confess a firm hope.
If we have a strong, sincere faith, we can receive a firm hope in Christ, who promises eternal life to everyone who completes his life in faith in Him, steadfast in His holy Church.

entries.section: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

paragraphs.text: The Apostle calls us to take care and to encourage one another in our love for others, in serving them and in doing all works of mercy.

entries.section: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

paragraphs.text: We must not neglect spiritual gatherings, nor attend them as a mere performance of duty, but use them to teach and exhort one another to grow in the spiritual life in preparation for eternity. Our encouragement of one another increases as much as we sense the approach of the coming of Christ, and that the time of the end of our life in this world is not known.

We note here that St. Paul stresses the importance of fellowship and the one body in encouragement and in giving patience in tribulation, since the Christian Hebrews were exposed to persecution from the Jews. So each one's encouraging the other gives steadfastness and patience in faith, for a person feels that there is someone standing beside him in the spiritual striving, and so he is encouraged and made steadfast in his Christ, being persecuted by the Jews.

Give me, my God, a spirit of positiveness, that I may stand firm and make those around me firm. Grant that people may see in me a steadfast branch in Your vineyard, so that I draw them by my sweet fruits from the work of Your Holy Spirit. Grant me to remember how much I promised You in the confession of my Baptism, to live with You and to receive You, renouncing all the thoughts of the evil enemy with all steadfastness and without wavering.

entries.section: (4) The warning against apostasy

paragraphs.text: "If we sin wilfully": this means apostasy from Christianity and returning to Jewish worship because of the persecution by the Jews, and it can also mean persisting in any sin.

He warns the believers against apostasy from the Christian faith, because the Jewish animal sacrifices will not profit us, and we will be deprived of the redemption of Christ and His atoning sacrifice.

entries.section: (4) The warning against apostasy

paragraphs.text: Whoever persists in rejecting Christ has nothing awaiting him but God's judgment of him on the last day, which is a terrible judgment, and He stands against him with great zeal to cast him into the eternal torment prepared for the wicked and those who reject Christ.

entries.section: (4) The warning against apostasy

paragraphs.text: The Law in which the Jews believe prescribes the putting to death of whoever transgresses it if the sin is proved against him by the testimony of two or three, and no excuse avails or finds pity. This is so that the Law may proclaim the fear of God and respect for the commandment (Mt 18:16).

entries.section: (4) The warning against apostasy

paragraphs.text: St. Paul shows the hideousness of the sin of him who denies the faith: he treads underfoot Christ and despises His precious redeeming blood by returning to animal sacrifices, and he scorns the grace of the New Testament, which he received in the Holy Sacraments and experienced in his life. If the punishment for transgressing the Law is death, then the rejection of Christ deserves an eternal torment whose hideousness cannot be imagined. And here he declares the divinity of Christ by saying "the Son of God."

entries.section: (4) The warning against apostasy

paragraphs.text: St. Paul cites the word of God in the Book of Deuteronomy (Deut 32:35, 36), that God judges the wicked and takes vengeance on them. And he uses a human feeling, namely vengeance, to stress the divine punishment of those who reject Him.

entries.section: (4) The warning against apostasy

paragraphs.text: God is just, living forever and very great; so whoever denies Him and persists in disobeying Him must in the end fall into His hands on the Day of Judgment, and receive a fearful punishment beyond all imagination. After St. Paul persuaded the Jews that all their rites signify Christ, he warns them lest the believer of Jewish origin fall away from Christ and receive an eternal punishment and torment. The Apostle declared all this to rescue those who have fallen away from destruction, that they might return by repentance.

Remembering the judgment alerts us to return from our sins and our negligence. God's mercy is for those who fear Him and not for those who despise Him, and our weakness does not hinder His work, but our contempt and persistence in sin is what exposes us to divine punishment.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: After the severe warning, he softens his words by encouraging them, declaring their virtues, namely their patience in the tribulations they met from non-Christians after their Baptism. Their steadfastness and patience call them to return to Christ and to stand firm in the faith.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: You were famous for the virtue of endurance of sufferings, and in this you shared with the martyrs and the saints who endured torments, such as Stephen.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: For I do not forget that you encouraged me during my imprisonment and trial and had compassion on me, and that you even rejoiced when you were subjected to the seizure of your possessions, not caring about what is yours on earth but about the eternal portion you have in heaven, prepared for you, which the moth does not eat and thieves do not steal, as they do the earthly portion.

Yes, Lord, teach me not to care about what is mine when it is taken from me for the sake of Your name. Teach me to give up even my lawful right if it hinders me from the glory of Your name, looking to heaven, my original homeland, from which I came, born of You, and to which I shall return to You by Your grace and the work of Your forgiving blood and Your body given for me.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: Do not neglect your faith in Christ, who grants you blessings on earth and in heaven .. many blessings that cannot be expressed.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: He calls them to patience in enduring persecutions, encouraging them with the receiving of God's promises of blessing, His support of them during their striving, and their reward in the Kingdom.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: This is because the Lord will come very soon if we compare our temporary earthly life with the blessed eternity, for the life of men on earth, however long, is nothing before eternity, which has no end. So Christ will come soon and glorify His children with Him in heaven.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: That you may continue the life of righteousness and holiness, hold fast to your Christian faith. And God declares in (Hab 2:4) that the just shall live by faith. St. Paul the Apostle goes on to make clear God's displeasure with the righteous man if he falls away from his righteousness and his faith, to warn the Christians of Jewish origin lest they fall away from their faith.

entries.section: (5) Steadfastness in Christ

paragraphs.text: In conclusion, he encourages them to remain steadfast in the faith by saying that they are not among those who fall away, for whom destruction waits, but that they are steadfast in faith in Christ.
Faith

entries.section: (1) Faith and creation

paragraphs.text: St. Paul the Apostle ended the previous chapter with the importance of steadfastness in faith in Christ so that we may endure sufferings and persecutions. And this chapter begins with a definition of faith, saying that it is trust in the power of God, which gives us what we do not see with our eyes now but hope for from His grace, and that this faith is what has distinguished the children of God throughout history since the beginning of creation.

entries.section: (1) Faith and creation

paragraphs.text: We believe first in God, the Creator of all creatures, whether in the world of earth or heaven, and that they came to be out of nothing by the command of God and not out of anything previously existing.

If God created everything out of nothing, then He is able to create in me a new heart that loves Him and seeks Him, and to give me an inclination to serve those around me and strength to help them. So I trust in Him and go forward boldly, whatever my weakness.

entries.section: (2) The faith of Abel, Enoch and Noah

paragraphs.text: Abel learned from his father Adam that he would gain God's favor by offering animal sacrifices, just as God slew an animal and clothed his parents with its skin, so that they were covered (Gen 3:21), and taught them that by offering sacrifices they would gain God's favor. Because of Abel's faith and obedience he was justified before God, whereas Cain did not believe God's teaching and offered of the fruits of the ground. Therefore, after Cain killed Abel, his faith continued to bear witness for him (Gen 4:4).

entries.section: (2) The faith of Abel, Enoch and Noah

paragraphs.text: Enoch, who was the seventh person from Adam, lived a life pleasing to God, and because of his great godliness God took him up alive to heaven, and he still lives there in a miraculous way, and will come down to earth shortly before the end of days (Gen 5:22, 24). Jesus the son of Sirach testified to his pleasing God (Sir 44:16). (The Book of Jesus the son of Sirach is one of the canonical books which the Protestants removed.)

entries.section: (2) The faith of Abel, Enoch and Noah

paragraphs.text: Paul was influenced by the words of Jesus the son of Sirach, and said in this verse that faith is the means to a life pleasing to God, which in the end receives the eternal reward.

entries.section: (2) The faith of Abel, Enoch and Noah

paragraphs.text: When God declared to Noah that He would destroy the world by a flood, he believed God's word and made an ark, the building of which took 120 years. It was a means of preaching, that men might repent, but they did not believe, so this ark became a judgment on them, while he was justified by his faith and had a portion in the Kingdom (Gen 6:13, 22).

Faith begets obedience to the commandments of God, so receive His commandments however hard they seem, confident of His help, which assists you to carry them out, and your heart will be filled with peace and you will be assured of a blessed eternity.

entries.section: (3) The faith of Abraham

paragraphs.text: God commanded Abraham to leave his family and his city, Ur of the Chaldeans, which lies between the two rivers in Iraq, and to go out to the wilderness of Canaan, which he did not know, promising him to give it as an inheritance to him and his seed. He believed God's word and obeyed him, and left the populous place where he had lived since his childhood and went out into the unknown, confident that this was the best because it was God's command (Gen 12:1).

entries.section: (3) The faith of Abraham

paragraphs.text: Despite God's promises to Abraham of the inheritance of the land of Canaan, he did not cling to material goods but lived as a stranger, he and his sons Isaac and Jacob. They dwelt in tents, not built houses, as proof of their being strangers to this world, because they were attached to the abiding city, which is the Kingdom of Heaven, which God founded and which lasts forever.

entries.section: (3) The faith of Abraham

paragraphs.text: Sarah also believed God's promise to her that she would conceive and bear, although her age had become ninety years and she had lost the human ability to bear children.

entries.section: (3) The faith of Abraham

paragraphs.text: "One": Isaac.
"As good as dead": Sarah's womb, unable to bear children.
God gave Sarah, from her womb, which by reason is considered dead, a son, Isaac, and from him came the people of Israel, great in multitude like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

entries.section: (3) The faith of Abraham

paragraphs.text: The first fathers believed in the Kingdom of Heaven and that it is the true life with God, so they were strangers to the material things of the world, and took nothing of earthly possessions, and their hearts were attached to eternity, so they passed quickly through this world to reach the Kingdom.

entries.section: (3) The faith of Abraham

paragraphs.text: The fathers' being strangers to the world declares their faith in another homeland, not earthly, and since they did not cling to the promised land nor to material goods, they declared their attachment to the heavenly homeland. For the sake of this great faith God is not ashamed to be called their God (Ex 3:6), and He prepared for them the heavenly city, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (3) The faith of Abraham

paragraphs.text: God tested Abraham to prove his faith and to show his greatness, and asked him to offer his only son Isaac as a sacrifice. Abraham obeyed, believing that God was able to fulfill His promises of many descendants through Isaac, since God is able to raise from the dead. And just before he slew his son, God stopped him and redeemed him with the ram. Thus the great faith of Abraham appeared, and the sacrifice of Isaac was an example and type of Christ the Redeemer on the Cross: Isaac returned alive because God redeemed him with the ram, but Christ died on the Cross and rose alive on the third day.

Your attachment to heaven makes you give up material things easily in order to gain your peace and the peace of those around you, and this increases your spiritual activity, whether in worship or in service.

entries.section: (4) The faith of Isaac, Jacob and Joseph

paragraphs.text: Isaac believed God's promise, at the birth of his children, that the elder would serve the younger (Gen 25:23). So he blessed Jacob his younger son despite his weakness and his lie, and promised him that he would be the father of a great posterity because he would repent and live with God, unlike Esau, who lived far from the worship of God, so Isaac did not give him the blessing he sought.

entries.section: (4) The faith of Isaac, Jacob and Joseph

paragraphs.text: By faith Jacob, the father of the tribes, blessed Manasseh and Ephraim, the sons of Joseph, placing his hands crossed (in the form of a cross) so that his right hand would be on the head of the younger. This was contrary to what was customary, so that Joseph tried to place his father's hands in the usual way, thinking that his father had made a mistake in the placing (Gen 48:18). But Jacob did this by faith, by God's revelation to him that the younger brother would be greater as a people. Therefore he placed his hands in the form of a cross, so that his right hand was on the head of the younger, Ephraim, and his left on the head of the firstborn, Manasseh, worshipping God in his bowing, as if he saw God who made these revelations to him. So he bowed down with the little strength he had, an old man, leaning wholly on the top of his staff.

entries.section: (4) The faith of Isaac, Jacob and Joseph

paragraphs.text: Joseph believed God's promise to Abraham that his seed would be strangers in Egypt and then return to the land of Canaan (Gen 15:14). So despite his great position in Egypt he asked his brothers and their descendants that when they departed from Egypt they take his bones with them, and that was about 400 years after these words.

Believe God's promises to you in the Holy Bible, and do not be troubled by the wars of the devil nor occupied with the passing delights of the world, but care for your spiritual life and the salvation of your soul at all times.

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: Despite Pharaoh's command to cast the male children into the river (Ex 1:22), the parents of Moses believed in God's power to preserve them and their son, and hid him three months, against the king's commands.

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: Moses was the son of Pharaoh's daughter, and so was considered the heir to the throne and could become king over Egypt or at least one of the great men of the state. But since he believed in God, he left the palace and went down to share with his people in humiliation and slavery until God would free them, knowing that all earthly lusts and sins pass away, whereas life with God lasts forever.

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: Faith is what lifted Moses above being dazzled by the title of son of Pharaoh's daughter and made him see this humiliation and reproach, which is after the pattern of the Lord Christ's humbling Himself for us from the throne of His glory, as a wealth with which all the treasures of Egypt cannot compare. This is because faith made him not care for temporary wealth but care for the eternal recompense from the hand of God, which is more lasting and better.

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: After God struck the land of Egypt with the ten plagues, Pharaoh yielded to the command of the Lord, and Moses left Egypt with power and did not fear Pharaoh, but on the contrary Pharaoh was afraid of him, because Moses saw God whom Pharaoh did not see. He was able to divide the Red Sea and cross it, while Pharaoh and all his army were drowned (Ex 14).

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: Moses believed God's promise to preserve them from the angel who destroyed the firstborn of Egypt, so he kept the Passover and sprinkled the doorposts with the blood of the Passover lamb as God said, so that the destroying angel would not harm them (Ex 12:21).

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: Moses and the children of Israel believed God's command when he struck the Red Sea, and it divided into two halves and the water became like a wall to the right and to the left. The people crossed in faith on the ground of the sea floor, which had become dry, and reached the other shore. But the hardness of the Egyptians' hearts made them follow them, and when they were all in the sea Moses struck the water and it returned to its place and the whole army of the Egyptians was drowned (Ex 14:22).

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: Jericho, the fortified city that faced the children of Israel under the leadership of Joshua after their crossing of the Jordan River, had its walls fall by the faith of the children of Israel, for all they did was to march around it for seven days as God commanded them (Josh 6:12-20).

entries.section: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

paragraphs.text: By faith Rahab, the sinful woman known in the city of Jericho for harlotry, did not perish with those who did not believe. This was because she believed in God and showed her faith by receiving the two spies and not telling the king of Jericho about them, but misleading the king's soldiers who were searching for them (Josh 2:1).
Faith makes you not fear the threats of people or the problems that meet you, so trust that your God fights for you and protects you, whatever the power of those who wrong you.

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: St. Paul the Apostle also declares that faith is the foundation of the life of all the saints in the Old Testament and that time is not enough to show their faith. Among their examples are Gideon the judge, who rescued the people of Israel from the Midianites (Judg 6:11); Barak, who delivered the children of Israel from Sisera, the commander of the army of the Canaanites (Judg 4:6); Samson, the vanquisher of the armies of the Philistines (Judg 13:24); Jephthah, who rescued the children of Israel from the children of Ammon (Judg 11:1); David, the righteous king, the psalmist of Israel (1 Sam 16:13); and Samuel, who stood before all the people of Israel when they wished to appoint an earthly king and opposed them by faith, looking to the King of kings and Lord of lords (1 Sam 8:6); and the rest of the prophets, who prophesied by faith about things that had not yet come.

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: St. Paul the Apostle moves from mentioning examples of the heroes of faith to the works of faith, and mentions:
1- "Subdued kingdoms": such as Samson (Judg 15:15).
2- "Wrought righteousness": they lived a holy, pure life, such as David.
3- "Obtained promises": by faith they were able to obtain what they were promised, such as Gideon (Judg 8:11).
4- "Stopped the mouths of lions": such as Daniel (Dan 6:22).

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: 5- "Quenched the violence of fire": it could not burn them, such as the Three Youths (Dan 3).
6- "Escaped the edge of the sword": such as Esther and Mordecai (Esth 8).
7- "Out of weakness were made strong": they were strengthened by faith, freed from their human weakness, such as Judith, who triumphed over the armies of the Assyrians (Jdt 14, 15).
8- "Waxed valiant in fight": they became men of might and strength in their wars, such as David and those with him (2 Sam 5:20).
9- "Turned to flight the armies of the aliens": such as Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, who defeated the Greek empire (the First Book of Maccabees).

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: 10- "Women received their dead raised to life again": by faith women were able to enjoy the resurrection of those who had died to them, such as the resurrection of the son of the widow of Zarephath of Sidon, whom Elijah the prophet raised (1 Kgs 17:22).

11- "Others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection": such as the many martyrs in the days of the Maccabees, among them the seven brothers and their mother (2 Macc 7).

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: 12- "Others had trial of cruel mockings": such as the Jews who fought alongside Judas Maccabeus, who after his death were seized and mocked (1 Macc 9:26).
13- "And scourgings": such as the seven brothers in the days of the Maccabees (2 Macc 7:1).
14- "Yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment": such as Joseph (Gen 39:20) and Jeremiah the prophet (Jer 37:15).

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: "They were stoned": as King Joash commanded the stoning of Zechariah the priest, the son of Jehoiada, because he rebuked the people for their sins that they might return to God (2 Chr 24:21), and Naboth the Jezreelite in the days of Ahab the king (1 Kgs 21:13). "They were sawn asunder": Jewish tradition mentions that Manasseh the king commanded that Isaiah the prophet be sawn asunder.

"Were tempted": such as the testing of Abraham by offering Isaac his son as a sacrifice (Gen 22). "Were slain with the sword": such as Ahimelech the priest, whom Saul the king slew because he fed David and gave him the sword and spear of Goliath (1 Sam 22:16). "They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented": such as Elijah the prophet, who lived stripped of possessions (2 Kgs 1:8), and as Micaiah the prophet, whom Ahab the king fed with the bread of affliction in prison, that is, he did not find his necessary food (1 Kgs 22:27).

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: "Of whom the world was not worthy": the heroes of faith mentioned above endured many sufferings for the sake of God and were weak only in appearance, but before God they are saints, higher than the world, and the world does not deserve their presence in it.

"They wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth": some of them lived in the deserts and mountains, keeping away from the evil of the world, which they rebuked, such as Elijah the prophet (1 Kgs 19:9) and John the Baptist (Lk 1:80).

entries.section: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

paragraphs.text: All these heroes of faith, to whose faith God bears witness, did not receive the promises on earth, but on the contrary endured many tribulations. But there awaits them, and awaits all of us when we complete our striving, an eternal Kingdom in which we shall enjoy together a happiness that cannot be expressed. They are waiting in the Paradise of Joy, the place of waiting of the righteous, until all the believers enter at one time into the Kingdom of Heaven.

The heroes of faith shone because of their striving and their endurance of many labors for God's sake. May we not grow slack in our prayers, our fasts and every good work, but also reject every sin, however pleasant and tempting, confident that our earthly labors are matched by heavenly glories.
Striving and serving others to obtain glory

entries.section: (1) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: "Cloud": he means the heroes of faith in the Old Testament who have come to be in heaven, so he expresses them as a cloud, and also because of their multitude, like the drops of water gathered together inside a cloud.
"Witnesses": the lives of these saints bear witness to practical faith.
"Compassed about us": the stories of their lives surround us and call us to imitate them, and they intercede for us so that we may be able to continue our striving.
"Let us run": we run like racers in a running race, that is, we hasten.

Therefore, brethren Hebrews, we have a great advantage and strength from the saints of the Old Testament, as a great cloud surrounding us who are on earth, from the good things and prayers of those who went before us and who bear witness to the victorious life of faith. Since we have this great cloud from which we draw strength, come, let us lay aside every weight of fear of persecutions and anxiety, because we have seen in the cloud those who had the weight of persecution but laid it aside by faith, such as David. This cloud also gives us strength to lay aside sin, with its many enticements and its ways which may beset us to make it easy for us to be far from God, and come, let us hasten to persevere in spiritual striving.

entries.section: (1) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: "The author and finisher of our faith": our God, who completes our salvation and is the foundation of our faith.
"Jesus": he mentions His name in the flesh to declare that He is the Son of Man who strove as we do and endured all sufferings.
"The right hand of the throne of God": the divine glory in the heavens, for the right hand means power and glory, and the throne means honor and perfect glory.

What encourages us to spiritual striving is imitating Christ, who set a goal before Him, namely our salvation, and endured the Cross, the sign of shame and disgrace. After He accomplished our salvation He rose from the dead and ascended to the heavens, that is, He came to be in the glory, which is a crown for everyone who completes his striving in this world.

entries.section: (1) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: The Apostle calls us to contemplate Christ's endurance of the opposition of the wicked, who tried many times to catch Him in a word and also tried to kill Him several times until they finally crucified Him. He endured them to teach us how to endure others, and He endured the torments of the Cross to complete our salvation. And as we always think of Christ's striving for us, we do not grow weary of enduring our sufferings or grow weak in continuing the striving, but persevere with confidence until we receive the heavenly crowns.

Take care to read the Gospels and the lives of the saints, so that you may be encouraged by the life of Christ and the life of His children to continue your spiritual striving, and God will send you consolations that support you, so do not be troubled however many your sins or your tribulations.

entries.section: (1) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: He encourages them to continue the spiritual striving by resisting sin unto death, so that they do not surrender to it however long the time, confident of the power of God within them, which is able to defeat the wars of the devil.

entries.section: (2) Chastening

paragraphs.text: You have pitied yourselves because of the chastenings to which you are exposed, not remembering what you learned from God in the Holy Bible, which exhorts you as sons, as in the Book of Proverbs (Prov 3:11): My son, do not despise the chastenings that come to you from the Lord, and do not grow weak or despair if rebuke is directed to you, for it is because of His love for you, because you are His son and He wants you in the best spiritual condition, and He allows you some sufferings as a fellowship in the cross of His beloved Son who was crucified for you and who endured many scourgings for you. So tribulations are by God's permission for the correction of our faults and the growth of our life.

entries.section: (2) Chastening

paragraphs.text: If you, beloved, accept chastening from God with patience, He is caring for you as His sons, because a father who cares for his children does not neglect their weakness and faults but corrects them by chastening.

entries.section: (2) Chastening

paragraphs.text: "Bastards": illegitimate sons.

If you reject the divine chastening that came upon all the children of God in the Old Testament and in which they shared for the correction of their lives and to bring them near to God, then your persistence in rejecting chastening declares that you are not sons of God. His use of the expression "illegitimate sons" matters to the Jews, who are careful about their genealogies in order to reach God; that is, he affirms that chastening is the proof of sonship. It is noted that the phrase "whereof all are partakers" is a parenthetical phrase which means that all the children of God accept chastening, but the meaning of the verse becomes easy if we say that those who are without chastening are not children of God.

entries.section: (2) Chastening

paragraphs.text: What is more, as a proof of the necessity of our submitting to God's chastening, we respect our fleshly fathers who rebuked us and punished us to correct our faults. How much more should we submit to God, the Father of our spirits in addition to our bodies, who permits trials to correct our spirits so that we may be able to live with Him and find our place in eternal life.

entries.section: (2) Chastening

paragraphs.text: Our fleshly fathers chastened us for a limited period until we became grown, and this chastening was according to their own opinion, which is liable to some error. But God chastens us by tribulations that we may profit spiritually, and He is holy and does not err; so by His chastening we are sanctified like Him, and we live with Him on earth and in heaven with all the saints.

entries.section: (2) Chastening

paragraphs.text: Tribulations with their sufferings cause a person sorrows, but they are temporary, and afterward they form in him virtues and spiritual fruits that remain with him forever to enjoy in the Kingdom. So chastening seems hard at its beginning, but afterward it produces peace and joy, while not accepting chastening gives a temporary pleasure and rest followed by sorrow and eternal destruction.

Trust that every tribulation you pass through is for your benefit, so do not murmur against it, but ask God's help to endure it and cling to Him more, and you will grow in your spiritual life and be happier in the end than those around you, because you are strong and your personality is more mature than many because of the tribulations you have endured.

entries.section: (3) Helping the weak and guarding against sin

paragraphs.text: "The hands which hang down": the slothful.
"The feeble knees": those who despair and have lost the ability to continue the striving.

Because of the tribulations and persecutions that God permits for the chastening of His children, some fall into sloth or despair. So St. Paul the Apostle reminds them of the words of Isaiah the prophet in (Isa 35:3) that they should encourage the slothful and the despairing so that they may be strengthened and continue their striving. And of course, before supporting others, a person encourages himself to rise from his sloth or despair.

entries.section: (3) Helping the weak and guarding against sin

paragraphs.text: "Make straight paths for your feet": walk uprightly.
"Turned out of the way": goes astray.
"That which is lame": the weak believer.
"Healed": his spiritual weakness is treated.

By your sound understanding of the word of God, walk uprightly, so that those weak in faith may imitate you and not depart from the way of God, but on the contrary be delivered from their weakness and become strong in faith.

Instead of judging sinners, take care to help them correct their faults by your prayers, your good example, the expression of your love for them, and alerting them to return from their faults if you have standing with them.

entries.section: (3) Helping the weak and guarding against sin

paragraphs.text: Keep your peace in your dealings with others, even if this requires some concessions and care in speech, while being careful about holiness and purity, so that you are without personal motives or exploitation of others, especially since this holiness or purity is a condition for seeing God and cleaving to Him.

entries.section: (3) Helping the weak and guarding against sin

paragraphs.text: "Fail of the grace of God": he loses the work of God in him because of his rejection of the grace of God.
"Any root of bitterness springing up": a plant whose taste is bitter appears and grows; he means a person's deviation from the faith or his persistence in sin.
"Trouble you": it distresses the believers.
"Be defiled": stumble and fall into sin.
He calls them to care for the believers so that they may be steadfast in the Church and enjoy the grace of God in it, and none of them deviate and distress and cause the others to stumble.

entries.section: (3) Helping the weak and guarding against sin

paragraphs.text: He warns them against persisting in sin and making light of it, such as persisting in uncleanness even to fornication, or as Esau did when he made light of his birthright and sold it for a meal of lentils.

entries.section: (3) Helping the weak and guarding against sin

paragraphs.text: When Esau came to his father Isaac asking the blessing of the birthright without right, because he had sold it to his brother Jacob, he was rejected by God, who allowed his brother to take the blessing, since his regret found no effectiveness and no place for changing his position, although he sought the blessing with tears, pleading to receive it, but he could not, because he did not weep for the sake of repentance but for the sake of the lost blessing.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: St. Paul the Apostle explains God's meeting with His people in the Old Testament to give them the commandments and the Law. He appeared in a great fire on the material, tangible mountain, and the mist was so thick that the place became dark, and a violent wind like whirlwinds surrounded the mountain, to declare the greatness of God and to establish the fear of Him in the hearts of His people.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: The people heard the sound of trumpets and were afraid, and asked Moses to speak with God and then tell them, because they could not bear to see or hear the fearful God (Ex 20:19).

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: God said to Moses that if any animal touched the mountain it must die, and they were not to touch it after its touching the mountain, but it was to be stoned or shot through with an arrow from a distance (Ex 19:13).

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: Jewish tradition mentions that the sight was so frightening that Moses himself, the great prophet, "he who spoke with God," said, "I exceedingly fear and quake."

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: The glory of the New Testament appears in the greatness of the Kingdom of Heaven, filled with angels, and this Kingdom is of course better than Mount Zion beside Jerusalem or the earthly city of Jerusalem that the Jews hold holy, but which is merely a symbol of the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: "Church": the assembly of the believers.

"Firstborn": in the Old Testament the firstborn had special blessings, and what is meant by the firstborn is the saints who completed their striving and receive spiritual blessings that cannot be expressed.
"Written": their names are written, that is, they are established.

"The spirits of just men made perfect": saints who completed their lives by the grace of God and so reached heaven. He describes the Kingdom as an assembly of believers upon whom the grace of God abounds, established in glory around God the just Judge, who rejoices in the spirits of His children around Him and completes all their deficiencies by His grace.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: "Mediator": Christ's mediating between man and God, and His making peace by His redemption of us and paying the debt for us.

"Blood of sprinkling": the blood of the blood sacrifices was sprinkled on the altar in the Old Testament, and the blood of Christ is sprinkled on us, that is, it atones for us and we receive His forgiveness through the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion.

"Speaketh better things than that of Abel": after Cain killed Abel, his blood proclaimed the sin of Cain, but the blood of Christ speaks better than Abel's, proclaiming the salvation and forgiveness of those who believe in Him.

He continues the comparison between the Old and the New Testament, showing the greatness of Christ the Redeemer as a mediator who reconciles man with God, and His blood gives salvation to His children.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: "Refuse not him that speaketh": do not reject the word of Christ.
"They": the children of Israel in the days of Moses.
"Escaped not": God was angry with them, so they died in the wilderness of Sinai and did not enter the promised land. "Him that spake on earth": Moses.
"Him that speaketh from heaven": Christ.

He warns them against falling away from the Christian faith by returning to the customs of the Jews, because if God was angry with the children of Israel long ago in the days of Moses when they rejected His word about entering the promised land and worshipped the golden calf and fell into many murmurings, so that they perished, how much more will be the punishment of him who falls away from faith in Christ, who comes from the heavens for our salvation.
Remember that the words of the Holy Bible are words from heaven that Christ sends you every day to guide your life, so take care to apply them and let them be your goal all day long.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants
