paragraphs.text: At the voice of God in the days of Moses the earth shook when He appeared on the mountain before all the people, and He will come once again at the second coming of Christ, and the material heaven and earth will shake and be changed, so that the new heaven and earth, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, may remain forever.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: While we prepare for the eternal Kingdom, we thank God for His grace, by which we are able to serve Him, and this service is characterized by the following:
1- It pleases God and is not according to our own desires.
2- With humility and the fear of God.
3- With righteousness, goodness and doing good.

entries.section: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

paragraphs.text: St. Paul declares the greatness and power of God, likening Him to a fire that consumes all evils and destroys those who resist, and he took this expression from (Deut 4:24). He destroys the evil that is in us when we repent, but for him who persists in evil, the eternal fire awaits.

The fear of God creates within us a rejection of sin and a distancing from its sources, and if we fall into it, we return quickly by repentance to be cleansed from it, so that we live always in purity and see God and rejoice in Him.

entries.section: (1) Love of others and chastity

paragraphs.text: The Apostle calls them to love others and to continue and grow in it.

entries.section: (1) Love of others and chastity

paragraphs.text: He alerts them to take care to entertain strangers, for it gives blessings to the one who does it greater than he imagines, such as Abraham and Lot, who entertained men and discovered afterward that they were angels; indeed, in the case of our father Abraham, God Himself was with the two angels (Gen 18:2; 19:1, 2).

entries.section: (1) Love of others and chastity

paragraphs.text: Remember those who are in bonds, and do not be in a high tower, separated from those who are in sufferings, whether bonds of imprisonment for the sake of the word of God or bonds of sins. Remember them in your prayers and in visiting them and helping them. Likewise, care for those who suffer a trial or tribulation in their lives, putting yourselves in their place so that you feel their sufferings.

entries.section: (1) Love of others and chastity

paragraphs.text: Marriage is a great sacrament in Christianity, higher in its meaning than all pagan ideas and other religions, since it is a union between the spouses accomplished by the Holy Spirit. So he requires the married to keep their conjugal relationship in a sound way and to keep away from every deviation against the commandments of God (Rom 1:26, 27) so that they do not defile their relationship. And he attacks strongly fornication and uncleanness of all kinds, because God will judge them and will destroy everyone who persists in them.

entries.section: (1) Love of others and chastity

paragraphs.text: He calls them not to be attached to money, that is, to keep away from covetousness, or getting money in an unlawful way, or relying on it before God, or being distressed at its scarcity, and to put in their hearts that God gives them what suffices them as He promised in the Book of Joshua (Josh 1:5), and not to worry or fear that what they have is not enough, because God gives them their sufficiency and guarantees it, so that they trust in Him like David the prophet (Ps 118:6).

entries.section: (1) Love of others and chastity

paragraphs.text: He alerts them to take care of their spiritual teachers, to provide for their needs, to submit to them, and to imitate their lives and their faith, whose reward is the joys of heaven into which they entered after their departure from this life.

May you learn from the fathers and spiritual guides at least one quality from each one, and take care about their guidance even if it opposes your purposes and mood, for it is spiritual experience and a message directed to you from God.

entries.section: (2) The sacrifices of the Old and the New Testament

paragraphs.text: The Lord Jesus Christ is constant and does not change; He is yesterday in the Old Testament and the same today in the preaching of the Gospel with the grace of the New Testament, and He is the true God who abides forever.

entries.section: (2) The sacrifices of the Old and the New Testament

paragraphs.text: The proof of steadfastness in God in ancient times was the eating of the Passover and the peace offerings, which were a type of the sacrifice of Christ in the New Testament, in which we are made steadfast by His grace when we partake of His most holy Body and Blood. So he alerts them not to return to eating of the animal sacrifices according to the Jewish rite, for they are Jewish teachings foreign to Christianity which declare that the sacrifice of Christ is not sufficient for salvation, so these teachings must be rejected.

entries.section: (2) The sacrifices of the Old and the New Testament

paragraphs.text: The altar of the New Testament and what is offered on it, namely the Body and Blood of Christ, the priests and servants of the Jews are not permitted to eat of, because they believe that salvation is by eating the animal sacrifices and do not believe that salvation is by the blood of Christ alone, to which these sacrifices pointed.

entries.section: (2) The sacrifices of the Old and the New Testament

paragraphs.text: "The camp": the place where the children of Israel lived and pitched their tents around the tabernacle of meeting.

"The gate": the gates of the city of Jerusalem. He also affirms that the sacrifices of the Old Testament were a type of the sacrifice of Christ, for on the great Day of Atonement the high priest would enter into the Holy of Holies with the blood of the sacrifice, while the sacrifice itself was burned outside the camp (Lev 16:27). It is a type of Christ, who was crucified outside Jerusalem at the place of Golgotha in order to redeem and sanctify those who believe in Him (Jn 19:20).

entries.section: (2) The sacrifices of the Old and the New Testament

paragraphs.text: St. Paul calls the Christians of Jewish origin to leave the Jewish worship, whose center is Jerusalem, and to go out to the Christian worship, enduring insults from their Jewish brethren as Christ endured the shame of the Cross for us, because we ought to live with a mind of being strangers to the world and its lusts and positions, and endure tribulations in order to reach the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

Do not be troubled by others' opposition to you in your holding fast to your prayers and your attachment to the Church or your spiritual principles that you learned from the fathers, and trust that these insults are a crown of boasting for you. Do not be angry; you may explain your principles to them if they want to hear, and if they refuse, then be silent and endure for God's sake and do not waver from your principles, as Christ endured all insults for your sake.

entries.section: (2) The sacrifices of the Old and the New Testament

paragraphs.text: "By him": by Christ.
He calls us to new kinds of sacrifices in the New Testament which we are able to offer by the grace of Christ (Ps 51:16), and they are:
1- The sacrifices of the lips, that is, prayers, praise and thanksgiving.
2- The sacrifices of good works, that is, works of goodness and mercy.

entries.section: (3) Caring for the guides and submitting to them

paragraphs.text: "Not with grief": not suffering.

The Apostle calls them to obey the servants and spiritual guides who love them and regard their service as a responsibility before God for which they will give account, so that they serve them faithfully, because their not obeying them will weary them, and this makes God displeased with them, in addition to the fact that the guides will not be able to convey all the spiritual benefit to them.

entries.section: (3) Caring for the guides and submitting to them

paragraphs.text: With humility and love St. Paul, who is their father and spiritual guide, asks them to pray for him that God may give him wisdom in his service and his conduct, for he loves them and his conscience is sincere toward them. By this humility he completes the meaning of the previous verse, in which he requires them to submit to the guides, so that they would not think he wanted to lord it over them rather than seek their spiritual benefit.

entries.section: (3) Caring for the guides and submitting to them

paragraphs.text: He also asks for their prayers to ease his coming to them, for he longs to see them, and he feels that he is of Jewish origin and wishes to return to Jerusalem and Judea, where he lived and was taught.

entries.section: (3) Caring for the guides and submitting to them

paragraphs.text: "The God of peace": St. Paul was compelled in this epistle to refute the arguments of the false teachers who wanted to take the Christians back to Jewish worship, and they had opposed him greatly. Now he wishes that the believers may live in peace that God, the God of heaven, grants them, keeping away from arguing with these false teachers and from all the problems that arise with them.

"Brought again": he speaks of Christ as a man who needed God to raise Him from the dead, that is, His divinity raised His humanity. He wishes that the believers may live in peace from God, who is able to do all things, who raised Christ from the dead and who is the shepherd of our souls as a shepherd tends the sheep. And this peace helps us to concentrate on good works, which are the will of God in our lives and by which we please Him, and He helps us to complete them throughout our life and forever.

entries.section: (3) Caring for the guides and submitting to them

paragraphs.text: If St. Paul was compelled to refute the ideas of the false teachers and explain them in this epistle, he apologizes to the Christians of Jewish origin who read this epistle and asks their forbearance of these many words of his, which are very brief; and had he let himself explain, he would have written far more than this.
Be gentle in your speech with others, care about their feelings, and adorn yourself with words of apology and asking leave, so that you win your hearers.

entries.section: (4) Closing farewell

paragraphs.text: Let it be known to you, beloved, that our brother Timothy, whom you know well, has been released from his prison and will be with me when I come and see you very soon, if the Lord will and we live.

entries.section: (4) Closing farewell

paragraphs.text: He asks that his greeting be conveyed to their guides and servants, for they are responsible for the care of the Church among them, and also to all the believers to whom it may be hard to convey the epistle so that they may read it. And on the other hand he sends the greetings of all the believers around him in Italy, where he wrote this epistle.

entries.section: (4) Closing farewell

paragraphs.text: He wishes at the close of his epistle that the grace of Christ may always work in them. And he makes clear that he dictated this epistle to Timothy when he was in Rome, which is in Italy, because his eyesight is weak and he needs someone to write his epistles for him. And he mentions Timothy his disciple because he is known and accepted among the Jews, for his mother and grandmother were Jewesses (Acts 16:1-3), and this makes their acceptance of the epistle easy.

When you use a mediator between yourself and others, take care that he is accepted and loved by them, so that agreement may be made or matters between you and them completed, for a person is affected psychologically and accepts the words if they are from someone known and loved by him.
